Structure, marks, references, bindings and terms must survive the round-trip and must not be translatable as text
An import must report anything it could not place, rather than dropping it (**IMP-007**)
A translation job must be trackable: what was sent, when, to whom, and what has come back
A translation job must be trackable: what was sent, **which version of the source it was sent from**, when, to whom, and what has come back

An import must be checked against the source version it was sent from (LOC-033). Where the source has moved since, the import must never be applied silently: the conflict must be reported and the outcome chosen - accepted as a translation of the older version and marked out of date, rejected, or placed for review against the changed source - by a person, with the default declared as policy (LOC-036)

A bound value must stay inert through the round trip (LOC-020). Where a source returns display text that must appear in another language, it must be translated at resolution against a declared lookup - a vocabulary in **LIB** keyed by the value the source returned - and never by editing the binding or its result inside a variant. Where no lookup exists, the value must render in the language the source gave it and be reported as untranslated
Machine translation must be available as an assist, producing a draft variant rather than a finished one
Machine-translated content must be marked as such until a human accepts it, on the same terms as **GEN-022**
A machine translation must use the tenant's terminology, and must be checkable against it
Whether content may be sent to an external translation service must be a tenant policy, not a default
Accepting a machine-drafted variant must be an audited act naming the person who accepted it (**GEN-024**, not only GEN-022's marking), and who may perform it must be a permission (**IAM**)
A field must be a tenant-wide definition with a stable identifier, a name, a data type and the validation its values must satisfy. A field grouped by more than one schema must be one field

The data types a field may take must be a closed set - text, number, date, time, date and time, true or false, and user - and a field must declare whether it holds one value or several. Adding a data type must be a product change, not a configuration option
A date-and-time value must carry its offset from UTC, so that it names one instant. A date and a time must carry no offset

A user field's value must be a user of this tenant, and must remain readable - shown as no longer active - after that user is de-provisioned (**IAM-008**). A value must never become empty because the user it names has left
A user field's value must be a user of this tenant
A user field's value must remain readable - shown as no longer active - after that user is de-provisioned (**IAM-008**). A value must never become empty because the user it names has left

A field holding several values must hold no value twice and must keep its values in the order they were given, and must be able to declare the most values it may hold. For such a field, required must mean at least one value, and a default must be a list of values

A field must be able to draw its permitted values from a vocabulary (**LIB**) rather than taking free text, whether the vocabulary is maintained in the tenant or takes its values from an external source (**LIB-058**). _Replaces TPL-008 and LIB-021, which said this twice_

A field drawing on a vocabulary whose values come from an external source (**LIB-058**) must be validated against the values held in the tenant and never against the source, so that neither authoring nor publishing depends on reaching it
Whether a value is valid must depend on its field alone: the same value for the same field must never be valid on one artifact and invalid on another
A metadata schema must be a named, versioned, tenant-wide definition grouping fields, managed and assigned as one unit. _Replaces TPL-007_
A schema must declare, for each field it groups, whether the field is required, its default where it has one, and whether its value is fixed (MET-033). _Replaces TPL-010_

A value a schema fixes must be taken from the schema's default, which a fixed field must have, and must not be editable on the artifact: an attempt must be refused, naming the field and the schema (MET-022). A field must be fixed wherever any schema applied there fixes it

Schemas must apply at exactly four places - a component, through its component type; a document, through its template's document-level assignments; a section, through its template's section-level assignments (**TPL-054**); and a relationship, through its relationship type (**REL-053**). Schemas applied at different places must never compose on one artifact
Where more than one schema applied at the same place (MET-034) groups the same field, the field must apply once, and must be required if any of those schemas requires it
Assigning a schema whose default for a field differs from the default of a schema already applied at the same place must be refused, naming the field and both schemas

An assignment must always take the latest version of a schema. A new version of a schema must be refused where its default for a field would differ from that of a schema applied beside it at any place, naming the field, the other schema and every such place, and where it would make an existing relationship invalid (**REL-054**)

An assignment must always take the latest version of a schema. A new version of a schema must be refused where its default for a field would differ from that of a schema applied beside it at any place, naming the field, the other schema and every such place
A new version of a field must be refused where it would make invalid the default of any schema grouping that field, naming the field, each such schema and its default

An assignment of a schema must be able to make an optional field required for that assignment, and must not otherwise alter the schema: not make a required field optional, change a default, fix or unfix a value, or change a field's validation
A component type must be a named, versioned, tenant-wide definition assigning zero or more metadata schemas, and must be distinct from the kinds of content a component holds
Every component must be of exactly one component type, chosen when it is created
A tenant must declare a default component type, which may assign no schemas, so that creating or importing a component always has a type to take
Every tenant must have a declared default component type, which may assign no schemas, so that creating a component always has a type to take

A component's fields must come from its component type and never from a document that references it, so that a component referenced by documents made from different templates carries the same fields in each
Changing a component's type must be an explicit, audited act, taking effect from the component's next version. Versions already cut must keep the type they were cut under

A component's metadata values must belong to its version: setting one must be a change to the component (**ADR-0006**), a version's values must never change once it is cut, and a baseline pinning the version must pin them (**VER-018**)
Metadata values must be held beside a component's content and never inside the content document (**CNT-144**)
Every component version must record the versions of the component type, schemas and fields it was written against, and must be validated against those for as long as it exists
A component's next version must be written against the current versions of its type, schemas and fields, so that a field newly made required is asked for the next time the component is edited

Where a component's next version is written against definitions under which a value's field no longer applies - its type changed, or a schema no longer groups the field - that value must not be carried into the version, and the version must record each value it did not carry, by field. A value whose field still applies must be carried unchanged
Changing a field, a schema or a component type must never make an existing component version, document or section invalid. _Replaces TPL-011, which said this of documents only_
Every change to a field, a schema or a component type must create a new version of it and must be audited
Every change to a field, a schema or a component type must create a new version of it
Validation must run while authoring, showing a missing or invalid field as it arises rather than only when publishing. _Replaces TPL-038, which said this of documents only_
A validation failure must name the field, the rule, the artifact, and the schema that applied the rule. _Replaces TPL-037_

Publishing a document must fail where any component version it references is missing a required field or holds an invalid value. Neither cutting a version nor designating a revision may be refused for that reason (**MET-Q03**)
The name of a field, of a schema and of a component type must each be unique within the tenant among definitions of its kind (**REL-040** is the same rule for a relationship type)
Managing fields, schemas and component types must be a permission of its own, grantable without tenant administration and separate from designing templates (**TPL-006**, **IAM**)

A field, a schema and a component type must each record where it is used - by schemas, component types, templates and relationship types, and through them how many artifacts - and changing one must show what the change affects before it is made (**DAT-016** is the same rule for a query definition)
Deleting a field, a schema or a component type that anything uses must be refused, naming what depends on it. It must never cascade

A field, a schema and a component type must each be deprecable: no longer offered for new use, still valid wherever it is used, with a replacement namable (**REL-037** and **LIB-055** are the same state elsewhere)
Publishing must run as four named stages - resolve, compose, paginate, render - each able to fail with diagnostics naming the stage

Every publishing failure must name the stage it arose in - resolving the document, composing it against its layout and theme, the engine, or storing the output - and the node, block, reference or definition it concerns
Resolve must apply transclusion, conditions, variables and bindings **before** numbering, cross-references and citations
The resolution order must be fixed, stated, and covered by a test, because every part of it has a failure that is invisible in the output
The resolution order must be fixed, stated, and covered by a test for each stage that exists, because every part of it has a failure that is invisible in the output
The resolution order's test must place and prove each stage as it arrives - bindings, transclusion, conditions and variables (PUB-002) - so that no stage joins the order untested

The resolution order's test must place and prove the binding stage (PUB-002): every bound value must be in the content before anything is numbered, a cross-reference resolved or a list generated, and the test must fail if the stage moves after any of them

The resolution order's test must place and prove the transclusion stage (PUB-002) when it arrives: before conditions (**REU-030**) and before anything is numbered, a cross-reference resolved or a list generated, and the test must fail if the stage moves

The resolution order's test must place and prove the conditions stage (PUB-002) when it arrives: before anything is numbered, a cross-reference resolved or a list generated (**REU-028**, **REU-029**), and the test must fail if the stage moves

The resolution order's test must place and prove the variables stage (PUB-002) when it arrives: before anything is numbered, a cross-reference resolved or a list generated, and the test must fail if the stage moves
An approved publication must be produced from a baseline, never from a live document
A preview may be produced from a live document, and must say plainly that it is a preview of unapproved content
Preview must use the same pipeline as publication, so that what a preview shows is what publishing will produce
A preview of a page range may be untagged where the engine cannot tag a partial document, but a publication must never be
Content must reach the publishing engine as data and never as source in the engine's own language, so that no content, however it is written, can execute
A layout must declare page size, orientation, margins and gutter
A layout must declare running heads and feet, with fields for at least the document title, the current section, the page number, the physical page count and the revision
A layout must declare page numbering, including restarts and a different scheme for front matter
A layout must declare the front and back matter a document carries: cover, approval page, contents, appendices
A layout must declare the front and back matter a document carries: cover, contents and appendices
A layout must be able to declare an approval page, showing the approvals recorded for what is published
A layout must declare the numbering schemes **STR** applies to sections, figures, tables and equations
A layout must be able to differ per output format, because a page has no meaning in some of them
A layout must be a versioned artifact, and a baseline must pin the layout version it published under
A layout must declare which output formats it supports, and publishing to one it does not must be refused rather than approximated
A layout must declare, as a BCP 47 tag, the language its generated words are in; publishing a document whose language that tag does not match as a language range must be refused, naming both
PDF must be a first-class output and must meet the fidelity bar in scope §4
PDF output must pass the publishing regression corpus - the engine spike's cases, grown by a case for every publishing defect found - on every change to the engine, the template or the pipeline
A footnote must appear on the page carrying its anchor
A table breaking across pages must behave as its table style declares (**STY-013**)
Widow and orphan control, keep-with-next and keep-together must be honoured

Widow and orphan control, keep-with-next and keep-together must be declared by style, passed to each engine as that engine's own rule, and shown by the publishing regression corpus to hold wherever the page allows

Widow and orphan control, keep-with-next and keep-together must be declared by style, passed to the PDF's engine as that engine's own rule, and shown by the publishing regression corpus to hold in the PDF wherever the page allows

Widow and orphan control, keep-with-next and keep-together declared by style must be passed to Word as Word's own rule, and the publishing regression corpus's cases, opened in Word, must show them holding in Word's own pages wherever the page allows
Typefaces must be embedded, subject to the licence recorded with the theme (**STY-041**, **STY-042**)
PDF/A must be producible where a layout declares it, for archival and submission
The document outline must appear as PDF bookmarks
Cross-references and citations must be internal links
A cross-reference in a paragraph's text - running text, a list, a quotation, a table's body cell, a footnote's text - must be an internal link to its target
A citation must be an internal link to its entry in the bibliography (**LIB**, **PUB-040**)

A citation in running text must be an internal link to its entry in the bibliography; one in a heading or a caption, whose words the contents and running heads repeat, is set without one (**LIB**, **PUB-040**)

Rendered output must be faithful to the composition that was paginated: line breaking, hyphenation, justification and glyph selection must be those the layout and theme declare (**STY**). A renderer must not re-break, re-hyphenate or choose a different glyph on its own
Hyphenation and line breaking must follow the language of the passage (**CNT-140**), not one language declared for the whole document

Where a typeface is substituted because its licence forbids embedding (**STY-052**), the document must be composed again against the substitute and the substitution reported on the publication. A substitution must never leave a page whose lines differ from the composition that was approved
Word must be a first-class output, not a convenience export
Heading numbers must be carried as a numbering definition Word understands, never as literal text in a heading
Footnotes must be real Word footnotes, numbered by Word
Cross-references must be fields Word can update, not the numbers they resolved to
Styles must map to Word styles, so that a recipient can restyle the document rather than receiving direct formatting
Suggestions should be exportable as Word tracked changes, and Word tracked changes should be importable as suggestions (**COL**, **IMP**)
Word output must be verified by opening it in Word, as a standing practice rather than a one-off, and every material change to the emitter must be re-verified
Word output must carry the resolved document's content, numbering and cross-references and leave pagination to Word; the PDF is the output a page number cites, and the publication record must say so
Contents, lists of figures and tables, and page references in Word output must be fields that Word refreshes when the document opens, never page numbers copied from the PDF
Equations in Word output must be native Word equations built from the same structure as the PDF's, never images and never a second conversion of the source

Where a style, a property or a construct has no faithful Word representation, publishing must either refuse it (PUB-014) or report it on the publication exactly as a lossy export reports (PUB-055). Word is not exempt from saying what it could not carry; what makes it first-class is that the answer is normally nothing, and **STY-081**'s conformance suite is what keeps it so
PDF output must be tagged and must meet PDF/UA

PDF output must be tagged and must conform to PDF/UA-1: every publication must pass veraPDF's PDF/UA-1 validation profile, and the Matterhorn Protocol checkpoints only a person can judge must be reviewed, and passed, on the publishing regression corpus whenever the engine, the template or the pipeline changes

PDF output must be tagged and must pass veraPDF's PDF/UA-1 validation profile on every publication; a heading deeper than six levels must be refused by name, since the engine cannot tag it as a heading under PDF/UA-1

The Matterhorn Protocol checkpoints only a person can judge must be reviewed, and passed, on the publishing regression corpus whenever the engine, the template or the pipeline changes, and the review kept with the release
Before each release, the Matterhorn Protocol checkpoints only a person can judge must be reviewed, and passed, on the publishing regression corpus, and the review kept with the release
Reading order must follow the document's own order, not the order things happen to be laid out in
Table header cells must be associated with the cells they describe
Publishing must fail where a figure has no alternative text (**CNT-022**)
The document's language and the language of any passage that differs must be carried into the output (**CNT-140**, **CNT-084**)
Word output must be accessible on the same terms, since a recipient may be reading it rather than the PDF

Word output must carry the structure a reader of the PDF is given wherever Word can hold it - headings, lists, tables with their header rows, figures' alternative text, languages, links and footnotes - and must name in the publication's report each structure it could not carry
Every Word publication must be checked automatically for accessibility, as PUB-091 checks the PDF, and the result retained with the publication
Accessibility must be checked automatically as part of publishing, and the result must be retained with the publication
Every PDF publication must be checked by veraPDF against its PDF/UA-1 validation profile as part of publishing, and the report must be retained with the publication

Where a preview is untagged by design (PUB-061), the reading context must say so to assistive technology as well as on screen, and must name the tagged output as the accessible path. A preview that is hostile on purpose must not be silently hostile
A table of contents must be generatable to a depth the layout declares
Lists of figures, tables and equations must be generatable
A glossary and a list of abbreviations must be generatable from the terms the document actually uses (**LIB**)
A bibliography must be generated from the citations present, formatted by the selected citation style (**STY-020**)
An index should be generatable where the layout declares one
All generated matter must describe the **resolved** document, after conditions have been applied
The same baseline, layout version and theme version must produce the same output
A publication must record the engine and engine version, and the template version, that produced it
A 300-page document must publish in under thirty seconds - a provisional budget, to be confirmed against real content

A declared 300-page reference document - prose, figures, tables, equations and footnotes - must publish to PDF, from the request to the recorded publication, at or under ten seconds at p95 with no measured sample above thirty, measured on a declared reference configuration recorded beside the result

A declared 300-page reference document - prose, figures, tables, equations and footnotes - must publish to PDF, from the request to the recorded publication, at or under ten seconds at p95 with no measured sample above thirty, measured on a declared reference configuration recorded beside the result; its conformance report (PUB-091) may join the publication after it is recorded, within five minutes
Anything that cannot be deterministic - a generation timestamp, an internal identifier - must be confined to places the layout declares
A publication must record the versions of everything that produced it: the baseline, the layout, the theme, the citation style, the pipeline itself

A publication's record must be no weaker than the baseline's pins (VER-018, **VER-055**) and must additionally identify any accepted generated content it contains, with the prompt, model and context digest retained for it (**GEN-023**, **GEN-046**)
Re-publishing a baseline years later must be possible and must produce the same document

A change to the pipeline, the engine, or any library either depends on must be checked against the recorded output of a fixed set of baselines, and a difference must fail before release rather than being found by a customer re-publishing (PUB-043, PUB-046)

An incremental compilation and a clean compilation of the same input must produce byte-identical output, so that reusing layout between compiles cannot introduce a difference nobody would look for (**PUB-Q05**)

Reproducing a publication must verify that what it pinned is what it got - the typeface files, the theme, the layout, the citation style and the engine version - and must fail rather than proceed with an equivalent (**STY-047**, **VER-018**, **VER-022**, PUB-063)
A publication must be retained, addressable by URL, and permissioned (**IAM**)
A publication not produced from a baseline must say that it is not approved, visibly on every page and once where assistive technology reads it, and its record must say so
A publication must be listed alongside the document that produced it, with who published it and when
A publication must be accompanied by the provenance of every bound value in it (**DAT-042**)
A publication must be immutable; correcting one must produce another rather than replacing it
A publication must be shareable outside the tenant only to a named recipient who has proved who they are, and never anonymously
Such a share must expire, and must be revocable with immediate effect
A recipient opening a publication that a later one has superseded must be told so, rather than reading a corrected document's predecessor without knowing
Every access to a shared publication must be recorded - who, when, and which publication - and must be reportable to the tenant that shared it (**LIF-026**)

A publication must be one baseline published by one act into a declared set of formats, and that set must be recorded with it. Publishing the same baseline to other formats later must produce another publication rather than extending this one (PUB-050)

A publication must include the PDF wherever anything in it cites a page (PUB-065). A Word-only publication must be refused where page citations exist, and must otherwise record that it carries no page-cited output

What becomes of retained publications when a tenant closes must follow **ADM-029** and **ADM-030** - offered in the export before closure, deleted with everything else after the grace period - and a share outside the tenant (PUB-057) must stop resolving when the tenant does

Expiry or revocation of a share (PUB-058) must stop further access within a stated bound, including a session already open: subsequent page loads, asset fetches and API calls must be refused rather than served from a session established while the share was live

Sharing a publication outside the tenant must create a named, time-bounded grant scoped to that publication alone unless the tenant grants more through the ordinary model (**IAM-071**). The recipient must prove identity before first access, the grant must appear in the external-access listing (**IAM-051**), and every access must be recorded (PUB-060)
Publishing must fail on any unresolved cross-reference, failed binding, unresolved citation, unresolvable footnote anchor, missing alternative text, missing style or unavailable typeface
Failures must be reported together, so that fixing a document is one pass rather than a sequence of single discoveries
A failed publish must produce no artifact at all, so that a partial document cannot be mistaken for a finished one

Publishing must fail wherever the resolved document cannot be faithfully rendered under its declared layout, styles and engine. The cases listed in PUB-072 are examples of that rule, never the whole of it

Publishing must fail on at least: an unresolved cross-reference, a failed binding, an unresolved citation, an unresolvable footnote anchor, missing alternative text, a missing style, an unavailable typeface, a missing glyph (**STY-049**), content that cannot be laid out - an unbreakable block taller than the area that must hold it, a figure that fits on no page at its declared size - and an equation neither output format can render. Each must name the block and the layout that could not take it

Publishing must be refused where the publisher may not read every component the resolved document contains, naming each such place in the outline and never the component; a publication must never contain what its publisher could not read

A resolved document in which no outline node survives conditions must publish the front and back matter its layout declares that has something to show - a cover, or a contents with entries - and must fail with a named error otherwise - never produce an empty artifact
Google Docs export must be labelled in the interface as lossy, and must not be presented beside PDF and Word as an equal
Any lossy export must report what it could not carry, at the time it is produced
HTML should be producible as a reading format, and is subject to the same accessibility requirements as the other outputs
A relationship type must be declared before it can be used
A type must declare a name, its permitted endpoint kinds, its direction, and its cardinality
A type must be able to declare a metadata shape that instances of it carry
A relationship type must be able to assign metadata schemas (**MET-005**), whose fields its relationships carry. A relationship type is one of the places schemas apply (**MET-034**)
A type must declare its inverse name, so that a relationship reads correctly from both ends
Relationship types must be extensible by a tenant administrator without a code change
A type in use must not be deletable, and changing its endpoints or cardinality must be refused where existing instances would break
Relationship types must be exportable and importable with the rest of a tenant's configuration

A type must declare a name, a stable identifier, its permitted endpoint kinds, its direction, its inverse name (REL-004), its cardinality (REL-042), whether it permits an artifact to relate to itself (REL-045), whether it is acyclic (REL-046), and the permission required at each end (REL-035)

Changing a type's metadata shape must be guarded exactly as its endpoints and cardinality are (REL-006): adding a required field, narrowing a field's type or removing one must be refused where existing instances would become invalid, and the refusal must say how many would

A change that would make an existing relationship invalid must be refused, saying how many would become invalid: changing a type's endpoints or cardinality (REL-006), assigning a schema to a type or removing one, and a new version of a schema or field the type assigns (**MET-035**) that adds a required field, narrows a field's type or validation, or removes a field. A relationship is edited in place rather than versioned (REL-033), so it cannot be judged by the definitions it was written against as a component version is (**MET-017**)

A type must be deprecable: no longer offered for new relationships, still valid on the instances that carry it, with a replacement namable (**LIB-055** is the same state for a vocabulary value). A type must not be permanent merely because it is in use
A type must be renamable, in both directions (REL-004), with its identifier unchanged - so that instances are unaffected and a name chosen badly is not carried for ever
A type's name must be unique within the tenant, and its identifier must be what instances reference, so that renaming one breaks nothing

Importing a type whose name already exists must be refused where the shapes differ and reported as a match where they are identical. It must never merge two shapes, and must never create a second type with the same name (REL-040)
An import that would leave existing instances violating an imported cardinality or endpoint rule must be refused, naming what would break, and must never be applied in part

Cardinality must be declared as the number of relationships of that type permitted per artifact at each end - one to one, one to many, many to many - and a second relationship of one type between the same ordered pair must be refused rather than created alongside the first
A relationship from an artifact to itself must be refused unless its type declares self-reference permitted (REL-047)
A type must be able to declare itself acyclic. Where it does, creating a relationship that would close a cycle must be refused at creation rather than merely stopped at traversal (REL-018)
A relationship must connect two artifacts of kinds its type permits, and must be refused otherwise
Relationships must be creatable between components, documents, assets, query definitions, terms, templates and publications
A relationship must be able to carry the metadata its type declares, validated on creation
Creating and removing a relationship must be audited
Cardinality must be enforced when a relationship is created, not discovered later
A relationship must be able to target a specific version of an artifact, or float at latest, as other references do
Deleting an artifact must handle its relationships explicitly - refused, or removed with a record - never left dangling

A relationship must be creatable between any artifact kind the product defines - the set **IAM** section 2 names - and the kinds a type permits (REL-008) must be drawn from that set rather than from a list repeated here

An existing relationship must be changeable where its type permits: its metadata edited, and either end re-targeted or re-pinned (REL-013). Every change must be audited with what it was and what it became (REL-011), so that no edit escapes the record by being an edit rather than a creation

A change to a relationship must be validated exactly as its creation was: endpoint kinds (REL-008), metadata shape (REL-010) and cardinality (REL-042) must all hold afterwards, or the change must be refused

Creating, changing or removing a relationship must require that the user may read both ends (REL-019) and holds the permission its type declares at each end (REL-047, **IAM-019**). Where a type declares none, edit on both ends must be required
Each end of a relationship must be able to pin a version or float at latest independently of the other (REL-013)

A floating end must resolve to the latest version at the moment a question is asked, and impact analysis must state which version it resolved to. An artifact deleted and recreated must never inherit the relationships of the one it replaced - those were handled when it was deleted (REL-014), and an identifier is never reused
A bulk create or delete must be atomic. Where it cannot be, it must report per member what happened and must never present a partial result as one outcome
Cardinality must be enforced atomically against concurrent creation, so that two relationships created at the same moment cannot both pass a limit that permits one (REL-012)
Neighbours of an artifact must be queryable, by type and by direction
Paths between two artifacts must be queryable, to a bounded depth
Every traversal must declare a maximum depth, and must fail rather than run unbounded
Traversal must terminate on a cycle rather than following it
Traversal must be filtered by the requesting user's permissions, and must not reveal the existence of an artifact they may not read
Where a path is truncated by permissions, the result must say a path was truncated without saying what was in it
Traversal must be available through the API and the MCP surface on the same terms (**API**)
A shortest path between two artifacts must be queryable, to a declared maximum depth, optionally along named relationship types
An interactive traversal must stop at a stated number of results, nearest first, and must say whether there were more
Neighbours, impact and shortest paths must return within a stated budget - provisionally p95 of 250ms, never above 500ms - for a tenant of a million components, whatever the user may see

Traversal and the graph view must be filterable by a relationship's metadata as well as by its type and direction (REL-015, REL-026), so that "superseded, since January" is one question rather than a list somebody filters by hand (**REL-Q06**)
"What would changing this affect" must be answerable, combining declared relationships with the references in **REU**
Impact must distinguish a hard dependency - a reference that would break - from a declared relationship that is informational
Impact must be presentable before a change is made, not only afterwards (**REU-008**)
A complete impact list, beyond the interactive limit (REL-030), must be obtainable as a report produced in the background, still bounded by depth and filtered by permission

Relationships must be viewable as a graph centred on one artifact, expandable outwards
The view must be filterable by relationship type, so that one question can be asked at a time
The view must degrade legibly where an artifact has many relationships, rather than rendering an unreadable tangle
Anything the view shows must be reachable as a query, so that the picture is never the only way to get an answer
A component must be referenceable by any number of documents, in any space the referrer may read (**IAM-016**)
Each reference must independently pin a version or revision, or float at latest, and which it does must be visible
A component must be referenceable more than once in one document, each occurrence distinct (**STR-010**)
A reference must resolve at read time and at publish time, never by copying content into the referring document
A reference whose target has been deleted or is no longer readable must fail the publish with a named error

A citation style must declare ordering, and how two sources that would render identically are disambiguated
Adding a citation style must be possible without a code change
A theme must bind one catalogue of each kind, and must be a versioned artifact

A theme must declare the formats a bound value is printed in, by its column type (**DAT-080**) - a number's decimal and group separators and its minus sign, a date's order and separator, a time's separator, a boolean's words - with overrides per language, and a value in content must be formatted from those declarations alone, the same in every output. A decimal must print at its declared scale, never rounded, and an instant in UTC; no locale data is read until a named, versioned source supplies these declarations (**LOC-038**) (**DAT-033**)
A template must bind a theme (**TPL**), and a document must take the theme its template binds
Moving a document to a different theme must be an administrative act, never an authoring one, and must be audited
Where a document references a style the theme does not contain, publishing must fail with a named error rather than substituting a default
A baseline must pin the theme version it published under, so that re-publishing an approved document cannot change how it looks

A draft must resolve against the theme version its document is bound to. Publishing a new theme version must not change how a draft looks under its author; moving a document to a newer version must be a deliberate, audited act (STY-026)

Before a new theme version is adopted, which documents it would change must be listable - STY-034 one level up - so that a theme bump is a decision with a visible blast radius rather than a surprise across a tenant
Adding a theme must be possible without a code change or a release, on the same terms as adding a style (STY-029) or a citation style (STY-023)
An administrator must be able to add a style to a catalogue without a code change or a release
A style added that way must immediately be selectable by authors and honoured by every output format
A style must not be deletable while anything references it, and its uses must be listable
Adding, changing and deleting a style must be audited, including what changed
A tenant must be able to restrict which styles authors may choose, so that a catalogue can hold more than a house style permits
Changing a style must show what it will affect before the change is made
The editor and the publisher must resolve the same style from the same catalogue, by the same rules
The editor must render typefaces, sizes, colours and spacing as the theme declares (CNT-082, CNT-097)
Where the editor cannot reproduce an effect because it depends on pagination, it must not approximate it silently; preview is what shows it (CNT-150)
Style resolution must be deterministic: the same content, style and theme version must always produce the same appearance
Every style property must be verified, by an automated suite, to render the same measured value in each output format that renders it - in the editor, in PDF and in Word

Every style property that both the editor and the PDF render must be verified, by an automated suite over the default theme and generated ones, to render in the editor at the value the PDF of the same content renders it: each length - where text starts, the step between two baselines, a size, a rule's width and where it runs, an image's size - within half a point, and each face, weight, posture, colour, underline and fill exactly. A difference is allowed only where STY-060's list of approved deviations names it

Every style property that both Word and the PDF render must be verified, by an automated suite, to render in a Word document at the value the PDF of the same content renders it, within the same tolerances as STY-080, a difference allowed only where STY-060's list of approved deviations names it

The editor must render every declared property of every paragraph and character style as the theme declares it, not a sample of them, so that STY-080's suite tests nothing STY-036 did not oblige (CNT-082, CNT-097)

The conformance suites (STY-080, STY-081) must each carry an explicit list of approved cross-format deviations - the Word typeface substitution in STY-052 is the only one today - and a deviation not on that list must fail. Determinism (STY-038) is a claim about one format given one input, never that every format renders identically

Where a style or a glyph will not resolve, the editor must render an explicit unresolvable marker rather than a silent default, so that the failure appears while somebody can still fix it (STY-027 and STY-049 are the publish behaviours)
A theme must declare the typefaces it uses, and each must be available in a browser, in the desktop shell, and in the publishing pipeline
A typeface that cannot be loaded must fail the publish, and must never be substituted silently
A theme must record the licence under which each typeface is held, and whether that licence permits embedding it in published output
Publishing must refuse to embed a typeface whose licence does not permit it, and must say so rather than quietly substituting
Typefaces supplied with the product must be open-licence, on terms that permit embedding in published output and redistribution with the software
A tenant must be able to supply its own typefaces, asserting the licence it holds them under, and the product must not redistribute an uploaded face beyond the tenant that supplied it
A typeface must be a versioned artifact, and a baseline must pin the exact files it published with rather than the theme version that named them

The default theme must cover the scripts the supported locales admit (**LOC-038**), the bidirectional text CNT-059 admits, and the mathematics CNT requires, because a face that cannot set them makes those requirements undeliverable
The default theme must cover the Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and Hebrew scripts, and the mathematics CNT requires, because a face that cannot set them makes those requirements undeliverable
The default theme must cover the Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew and Arabic scripts, set together in one paragraph as the bidirectional text CNT-059 admits

The default theme should cover the right-to-left scripts CNT-059 admits beyond Hebrew and Arabic, among them Syriac, Thaana, N'Ko and Adlam, so text in any of them publishes without a theme of the tenant's own.

The default theme should cover the Chinese, Japanese and Korean scripts and the Indic scripts, among them Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil and Telugu, so text in any of them publishes without a theme of the tenant's own.
Publishing must fail where any character in the document has no glyph in the theme's typefaces, rather than borrowing one from a face the theme never declared or setting an empty box
A typeface whose licence does not permit embedding in Word must declare a permitted face for Word output, and every publication using it must report the substitution

A typeface must be validated on ingest for the vertical metrics STY-054 depends on - ascent, descent and line gap - product faces when the product is built and tenant faces when they are supplied (STY-046). A face without them must be refused rather than tolerated
A catalogue must be exportable and importable, so that a house style can move between spaces and tenants
An import must report anything it could not represent rather than dropping it

An import must validate that every typeface, catalogue and style the imported catalogue references exists in the destination, and must report what does not at import time rather than leaving it to fail at publish (STY-027)
An exported catalogue must re-import into an equivalent catalogue, and that round trip must be covered by a test rather than asserted
A bound table must be able to select which of a result's columns appear, and in what order
A column must be able to carry a header different from the name the query returned
A column header must be able to carry a unit, and units must be presentable separately from values
A column the query did not return must fail rather than render empty (**DAT-086**)
Column width should be governed by the table style, with a declared override where a column must not wrap
Column width must be governed by the table style, with a declared override where a column must not wrap
A column must be able to declare that it must not wrap, and must then not wrap in any output
Column width must be governed by the table style, a column that must not wrap excepted (**TAB-052**)

Every declaration this area names - which columns appear and in what order, headers, units, width overrides, sorts, grouping, totals, formatting overrides, the empty state, any reshaping and the wide-table strategy - must live in the table's definition and must address a column by the key the query declares (**DAT-080**, **DAT-012**), never by its position in the result

Selecting the same result column more than once must be refused unless each selection carries a distinct header, so that a value shown twice - raw and rounded, say - is a deliberate presentation rather than a duplicated column
A table must preserve the order the query returned, unless it declares its own sort
A declared sort must be stable, so that two rows that tie do not swap between runs
Rows must be groupable by a column, with a group heading row
Totals and subtotals must be declarable per column, with the aggregation named
An aggregation must state whether it was computed here or returned by the query, because the two can disagree
A table returning no rows must render a declared empty state rather than a table with a header and nothing under it

Grouping must be declarable on more than one column, nesting in a declared order, and the relationship with a declared sort (TAB-007) must be stated: groups order first, and the sort applies within each group

A group heading must stay with the first row of its group, and a subtotal with the last row of its, across a page break. How that is achieved is the table style's (**STY-013**); that it must hold is this document's

A group heading must stay with the first row of its group across a page break, and a subtotal must never begin a page without its group's heading above it: kept with its group's last row, or beneath the heading repeated. How that is achieved is the table style's (**STY-013**); that it must hold is this document's
The aggregations available for a total or a subtotal must be a closed set - sum, count, minimum, maximum and mean - named on the column. Anything else must be computed by the query (TAB-020, TAB-N02)

A total computed here rather than returned by the query (TAB-010) must record its inputs and its rule in provenance, so that a number on the page that no query returned can still be explained (**DAT-085**)
Each column must take field formatting from the table style by type, and must be able to override it (**STY-014**)
Formatting must cover at least number, currency, percentage, date, time, duration and unit
Precision must be declarable per column, and must be applied consistently rather than following whatever the source returned
Rounding must be declared, and the rule must be stated rather than assumed
The presentation of a negative value must be declarable - sign, parentheses, colour - because conventions differ by discipline
The presentation of a null must be declarable and must be distinguishable from zero and from an empty string
Formatting must respect the document's locale for decimal and thousands separators and for dates
A formatted value must never change the underlying value, and provenance must record what the source returned rather than what was displayed

Where the table style and a column's override both declare a formatting property, the column's must win, property by property rather than wholesale: a column overriding precision keeps the style's currency symbol, its separators and its negative form (TAB-012, **STY-014**)
Converting a unit must be the query's work, never the presentation layer's. A unit declared on a column (TAB-003) labels the value the query returned and must not change it (**DAT**, TAB-N02)

Formatting must respect the locale of the language the document is published in (**LOC-028**, **CNT-140**) for decimal and thousands separators and for dates - not the reader's, because a published document has one locale
A numeric column must align on its decimal separator, and alignment by column type must come from the table style (**STY-012**) rather than being set per table
Pivoting and aggregation must be performed by the query wherever the source supports them
The presentation layer must perform only a declared, narrow set of reshaping: transposing a small result, and grouping as in section 4
Any reshaping performed here must be stated in the table's definition, so that a reader of the definition can see what the query did not do
Reshaping must never change the number of values, only their arrangement
A footnote must be anchorable to a cell by key value (**DAT-012**, **CNT-039**)
A footnote must be anchorable to a column and to the table as a whole
Table footnotes must be numbered in their own sequence, separate from the document's footnotes, as convention requires
A table must be able to carry a source note, stating where its data came from in the reader's terms rather than the system's
Conditional presentation - a threshold exceeded, a value out of range - must be declarable as a rule in the table style (**STY**)
Such a rule must not be authorable per document, so that two tables of the same kind highlight the same things
Emphasis must not be carried by colour alone, since it must survive monochrome printing and meet accessibility requirements
Header cells must be associated with the cells they describe, in every output (**PUB-032**)
A table's behaviour at a page break must follow its table style (**STY-013**)
A table too wide for its page must be handled by a declared strategy - rotation, scaling or splitting - not by silent clipping
A table must carry a caption, and must be numbered by the outline (**STR-071**)
A caption must be programmatically associated with its table in every output, not merely placed beside it (**PUB-090**)
Header rows repeated across a page break must be exposed to assistive technology as headers rather than as new rows of data (**PUB-031**, **PUB-032**)
A table must carry its role and reading order into tagged output, and a table rotated, scaled or split by TAB-033 must remain one table to assistive technology rather than becoming two unrelated ones
A table must carry its role and reading order into tagged output, and a table broken across pages must remain one table to assistive technology rather than becoming two
A table rotated, scaled or split by TAB-033 must remain one table to assistive technology rather than becoming two unrelated ones

A table's header rows must be associated with the cells they describe in every output. Its header columns must be associated wherever the output format can express a header column, and where a format cannot, the publication's report must say which tables lost that association (**PUB-032**)
A template must be a named, versioned artifact belonging to a space
A template must bind exactly one of each definition: metadata schema, structure outline, query set, presentation theme, publishing layout, prompt library
A template must **own** its metadata schema and its structure outline, and must **reference** the other four
A template must bind exactly one structure outline, query set, presentation theme, publishing layout and prompt library, and zero or more metadata schemas (**MET-005**)
A template must bind exactly one structure outline, presentation theme and publishing layout, and zero or more metadata schemas (**MET-005**)
A template must bind exactly one query set

A template's query set must be the query definitions its required components' bindings name (TPL-014), computed when it is resolved rather than declared, and must resolve before a document is made from it (TPL-004)
A template must bind exactly one prompt library
A template must **own** its structure outline, and must **reference** every other definition it binds, its metadata schemas included
A template must not be usable to create a document while any definition it references does not resolve
A template must be testable by creating a throwaway document from it, without that document entering the space
Templates must be permissioned separately from the documents made from them, because designing one and writing one are different jobs

Where a template needs no prompt library or no query set, it must bind a declared empty default rather than nothing, so that TPL-060 and TPL-061 hold and TPL-004 always has something to resolve (**TPL-Q01**)
Where a template needs no prompt library, it must bind a declared empty default rather than nothing, so that TPL-061 holds and TPL-004 always has something to resolve
A metadata schema must declare typed fields, each with a type, whether it is required, and its validation rules
A field must be able to draw its permitted values from a controlled vocabulary rather than being free text (**LIB**)
A schema must be able to apply fields at document level and at component level, since the two are asked different questions
A field must be able to declare a default, and whether that default may be changed after instantiation
Changing a schema must not invalidate documents already created against an earlier version of it

Each metadata schema a template assigns must declare whether it applies to the document or to the document's sections (**MET-034**), and may make an optional field required for that assignment and nothing more (**MET-009**)
A structure outline must declare the sections a document starts with, and their order
It must be able to mark a section as required, meaning a document may not be published without it
It must be able to declare a component that every document from this template includes - shared boilerplate, a standard methodology statement
It must declare what an author may change: whether sections can be added, removed or reordered
A starting outline must not be a document's outline. Once instantiated, the document owns it (**STR**)
A required component (TPL-014) must declare where it sits: at a position in the starting outline, or as document-level matter the publishing layout places (**PUB-088**)
A required component (TPL-014) must declare where it sits in the starting outline: at the start or end of a starting section, or at the start or end of the outline's front matter, body or appendices
A template must declare its parameters: name, type, whether required, and the permitted values or range of each
A document must not be creatable until every required parameter has a value
A parameter must be usable to seed metadata, to resolve variables, and to supply arguments to the queries the template's bindings run
A parameter's value must be recorded on the document, and must be visible and auditable afterwards
Whether a parameter may be changed after instantiation must be declared, because changing "the site this report is about" is not the same as correcting a typo

A template must declare what each parameter feeds: which metadata field it seeds, which variables take their value from it (**REU-018**), and which query arguments it supplies (**DAT-010**). A parameter with no declared use must be refused rather than accepted and ignored
A variable a parameter feeds must be one **REU** declares (REU-018). This area supplies values; it does not define the vocabulary or the resolution rules (REU-016, REU-036)

A parameter value that is present but invalid - the wrong type, outside its permitted range, or absent from its vocabulary - must be refused and named with the parameter, the rule and the value, through the API (TPL-026) exactly as in the interface (**MET-022**)
A parameter must be usable to seed a document metadata field when the document is made, and to supply arguments to the queries the document's bindings run
A parameter must be usable to resolve variables (**REU-018**)

A template must declare what each parameter feeds: which metadata field it seeds, and whether it supplies query arguments (**DAT-010**). A parameter with no declared use must be refused rather than accepted and ignored
A template must declare which variables take their value from each parameter (**REU-018**)
Creating a document must materialise the starting outline, seed its metadata, resolve its variables, and establish its bindings
Creating a document from a template must materialise the starting outline and seed its metadata
Creating a document from a template must establish its bindings
Creating a document from a template must resolve its variables

Creating a document from a template must establish what its variables resolve from - the parameters that feed them and the bindings its required components hold - and must name each variable those components hold that does not resolve yet, without refusing the creation

A template must be able to declare default values for a document's profile axes, and which axes a document from it must set. Instantiation must establish the profile from those defaults, from parameters or from a declared incomplete state, and must never leave it undeclared (**REU-022**)
Whether a binding's query runs at creation and is pinned, or stays live, must follow the binding mode (**DAT-034**) rather than being a template setting

A binding's query must run when a document is created from its template, and its result must be stored (**DAT-083**); the binding's mode, checked or pinned (**DAT-082**), must govern only how source revisions are looked for, and must not be a template setting
A failure during instantiation must leave no partial document behind
Instantiation must record which template, and which template version, produced the document
Instantiation must be available through the API as well as the interface, since creating documents is the commonest thing another system will want to do
Creating a document must record who created it and when, on the document and in the audit log (**LIF-026**, **LIF-027**), alongside the template version TPL-025 records
A throwaway test document (TPL-005) must be discarded when the test ends and must never become reachable. Anything it produced - a binding run, a derived asset - must go with it
A document must own its outline after instantiation, and must be able to depart from the template's starting shape
Departures must be listable: what this document has that the template does not, and what it lacks
A section the template marked required must not be removable without a stated reason, recorded on the document
Publishing must fail where a required section is absent

A component the template declared required (TPL-014) must not be removable without a stated reason recorded on the document, and publishing must fail where one is absent - the treatment TPL-029 and TPL-013 give a required section
Changing a template must not alter any document already created from it
It must be possible to list the documents created from a given template version
Moving a document to a newer template version must be an explicit, audited act, and must be refusable
Such a move must report what it will change before it runs, and must be abandonable at that point
A move that cannot be completed must leave the document exactly as it was

Moving a document forward (TPL-033) must bring its fields to the current versions of the schemas and fields its template assigns as well as its outline to a newer template version, and must be possible when only a schema or a field has changed. The report TPL-034 requires must name each field that changes and each value that would not be carried forward, as **MET-036** treats a component's
A document must satisfy the metadata schema its template binds, and publishing must fail where it does not
Validation failures must name the field, the rule and the document
Validation must run while authoring, not only at publish, so that a missing required field is known early

Validation must enforce the definitions as they were in the template version recorded on the document (TPL-025), not as they are now: tightening a schema or marking a new section required must not make existing documents fail (TPL-011, TPL-031). Moving to a newer version is the deliberate act in section 9

A document must satisfy the fields its template applies at document level, and each section the fields applied at section level, and publishing must fail where either does not (**MET-022** names each failure)

Instantiation must record on the document the version of each metadata schema and field it was created against. An assignment takes a schema's latest version (**MET-040**), so the template version TPL-025 records no longer decides which fields apply

Validation must enforce what is recorded on the document rather than the definitions as they are now: its outline and required sections as they were in the template version TPL-025 records, and its fields as they were in the schema and field versions TPL-056 records. Tightening a schema or marking a new section required must not make an existing document fail (**MET-019**, TPL-031). Moving forward is the deliberate act in section 9
Bulk generation must report success or failure per row, and must never leave a partially created document behind for a row that failed
A cohort created together must be identifiable afterwards, so that forty reports can be tracked, reviewed and published as a set
A bulk run must declare whether a failing row stops the run or it continues, the choice must be the requester's with a stated default, and the report must say which happened (**REU-033**)
An iteration must be an immutable, timestamped snapshot recording the identity of the editor who produced it
An iteration must be visible only to the editor holding the component's lock
Iterations must be retained until the component's next version is cut, and for a declared window after that
The retention window must be a tenant setting with a stated default, because a window nobody chooses silently becomes "for ever"
Iterations must not appear in comparison, in audit, or in anything a reader sees. They exist for recovery
A version must be an immutable snapshot, promoted from an iteration by a positive act
A version must record its author, the time, and an optional change note
A version must never be edited or deleted; correcting one must produce another
Versions must be numbered sequentially within their revision, and the pair must be presentable as `revision.version`
Every version must record the schema version its content was written against (**CNT-011**)
Documents, outlines, assets, query definitions, themes, layouts and templates must each be versioned by the same rules as content
Documents, outlines, assets, themes, layouts and templates must each be versioned by the same rules as content
Query definitions must be versioned by the same rules as content

Immutability must mean more than an absence of writes: every version must record a content digest over its canonical serialisation, and that digest must be recomputable from the content by anybody holding it, so that tampering is detectable rather than only forbidden
Every recorded time must be an absolute instant in UTC (**LIF-062**), and the order of a chain must come from its sequence rather than from the clock, so that skew cannot reorder history
A revision must be a designation applied to an existing version, not a second snapshot beside it
A revision must be created only when a lifecycle gate is passed (**LIF**), never by an author acting alone
A revision must record who designated it, when, and against which gate
Revisions must be numbered sequentially from 1, and something never issued must be presentable as revision 0
A revision must be immutable once designated, including its number
A baseline must be a named, immutable version of a whole document

A baseline must pin the exact version of every component, asset, query definition, theme, typeface, layout and citation style the document used, and the outline itself (**STY-047** is what makes a typeface pinnable)
A baseline must pin every bound value and its provenance, regardless of the binding's mode (**DAT-038**)
A baseline must record the conditions in force when it was taken, because a document has as many resolutions as it has profiles
Creating a baseline must be an explicit act, and must be possible automatically at a lifecycle gate
Creating a baseline must be an explicit act
Creating a baseline must be possible automatically at a lifecycle gate (**LIF**)
A baseline must be reproducible: everything it pins must remain retrievable for as long as the baseline exists
Deleting anything a baseline pins must be refused while that baseline exists

A baseline must also pin what VER-018 does not name and resolved output still depends on: the bibliography entries, terms and vocabulary values the document references (**LIB-004**), and the template version recorded on it with the definitions that version owned (**TPL-025**, **TPL-043**)

A baseline must also pin what VER-018 does not name and resolved output still depends on: the bibliography entries, terms and vocabulary values the document references (**LIB-004**), the template version recorded on it (**TPL-025**), and the versions of the metadata schemas and fields its document and sections were validated against (**TPL-056**). A component version already records the definitions it was written against (**MET-017**), so pinning the version pins those
A baseline must record a digest over the set of versions it pins, so that "these are the exact inputs" is one value somebody can check rather than a list they must compare by hand (VER-042)
A baseline's name must be unique within its document and must not be changeable after creation, because the name is part of what an immutable record is cited by

A baseline must be markable as superseded, recording what superseded it, and a superseded baseline must remain retrievable. Baselines accumulate by design - nothing deletes one (VER-023) - so the controls are that creating one is a positive act and that a list can be filtered by state
Who may read a version history, run a comparison or export a redline must follow the permissions of what is being compared (**IAM**), and an export must carry no content its requester may not read

Comparison must meet a stated budget for a document of several hundred components with a history of hundreds of versions - provisional, confirmed against real content, measured in production like every other budget (**ADM-016**)

Comparison must be available at three levels: **structural**, what moved, was added or removed in the outline; **content**, what changed inside a component; and **resolved output**, what changed in the published result
Comparison must be possible between any two versions of a component, and between any two baselines of a document
Comparison must be possible across a template version change
A block that moved and was reworded must report as one change, not as a deletion and an insertion
Matching must use block identity where it exists, and content similarity where it does not
Every reported change must state how it was matched - by identity or by similarity - because a reader needs to know how far to trust it
A comparison must render as a redline, and must be exportable
Resolved-output comparison must catch changes caused by data, conditions or definition versions rather than by anyone editing

Comparison must be possible between two baselines of a document created under different template versions, and must separate what differs because a definition changed from what differs because somebody edited (VER-031's distinction, applied to a template's definitions)
Restoring an earlier version must create a new version whose content matches it. Nothing must ever be rewritten
A restore must record what it restored from, so the history reads as a decision rather than a mystery
Restoring must be refused where it would leave a baseline unable to resolve
An author must be able to preview what a restore would produce before it happens

Restoring must be refused where the restored content would reference something that no longer resolves - a component version since deleted, an asset removed - and the refusal must name what is missing. A restore adds a version rather than rewriting one, so it can never leave an existing baseline unable to resolve (VER-022, VER-032)
Versions, revisions and baselines must be retained for as long as the tenant keeps its content, subject to policy (**LIF**)
Retention and legal hold must be able to prevent deletion of anything a baseline depends on
Erasure of personal data must be reconcilable with immutable history by design, not by exception - what is erased and what remains must be stated

Deleting a component or a document must state what happens to its version chain: the chain must be retained under retention policy (**LIF-024**) and remain readable to audit, or the deletion must be refused. A chain must never be left orphaned - unreachable and undeleted

Where a chain is retained after the artifact it belonged to is deleted, what remains must be stated: its identity, its versions and the audit of them, with content removed only where erasure required it (VER-038, **LIF-024**)
Data derived from a version - an embedding above all - must record the model and the model version that produced it
Re-deriving must insert new derived data and must alter no version, so that changing model is an operation rather than a rewrite of history
A baseline must remain re-publishable on the engine version recorded with its publication (**PUB-063**) for as long as the baseline exists

The engine versions a baseline may need must be retained and runnable for as long as that baseline exists, and the cost of keeping them must be visible to whoever sets retention (**PUB-063**, **ADM**)

nonRequirements.statement: **No standing support access to tenant content** (ADM-023)

**No cross-tenant reporting** of content, or of product analytics identifying individuals or unrelated tenants, other than aggregates that identify nobody. Administrative and cost reporting across the tenants of one customer organisation is permitted to that organisation's own administrators (**IAM-068**, **IAM-069**), because they are one customer looking at themselves
**Not a billing system.** Usage is measured and reported here; invoicing is somewhere else
**No configuration only reachable by the vendor.** Anything a tenant is entitled to change, a tenant administrator can change
**Not a notification system.** This area decides what is worth alerting on and who should receive it; the inbox, the email and the delivery are **COL**'s (COL-033 to COL-036)
**No MCP surface generated from the API** (API-018)
**No privileged internal API** that the product's own clients use and others cannot (API-001)
**No arbitrary code execution as an extension point.** Extensions are declared and sandboxed, or they are not extensions
**No GraphQL surface alongside the REST one**, unless something forces it. Two APIs are two contracts and two sets of bugs

**No unattended bulk import through the API.** Bringing foreign content in is **IMP**'s attended flow (IMP-001 to IMP-003): a proposal a person accepts, and a report of what was dropped. An endpoint that skipped it would skip the person
**Not a digital asset management product.** This manages the assets used in documents, not a media library for a business
**No image editing.** Cropping, retouching and annotating happen elsewhere; an asset arrives finished
**No arbitrary file storage.** An asset is something content references, not an attachment locker
**No embedding of an original where a derivative will do**, and no derivative that cannot be regenerated

**No typeface, font size or colour _chosen by the author_.** The editor renders the theme's typefaces at the theme's sizes (CNT-097) - what the author cannot do is pick a different one. Narrower than "no styling" on purpose - see CNT-035
**No page geometry in content.** Page size, margins, running heads and columns belong to the publishing layout. Whether a forced page break is an exception is **CNT-Q07**
**No free-form drawing or diagramming.** A figure references a managed asset produced elsewhere
**No embedded spreadsheets or live formulas.** Computation belongs in the query layer
**No arbitrary HTML or raw markup escape hatch.** It would defeat every guarantee in section 3
**No per-author formatting preferences.** Two authors editing one document must produce content that looks the same
**No tables or images inside footnotes** (CNT-129, which superseded CNT-040)

**No per-document override of a theme's styles.** Where a document needs a different look it uses a different theme, which an administrator configures. Otherwise every document drifts into being its own theme

**No headings in component content.** A component carries no heading, because the outline owns structure and its titles (**STR**) - and because a component that knew its own heading level could not be used at two depths. A decision, not an omission

**No link to content inside the product expressed as a URL.** An internal target is a cross-reference (CNT-027), which survives a move, a rename and a renumber. A URL to a component would be a second, weaker way of doing the same thing
**No real-time character-level co-editing.** Scope §9 decision 4; the parallelism authors want is across components (**COL-011**)
**No document-level locking.** It defeats the point of components
**No comments in published output** (COL-019)
**No anonymous review.** Every comment, suggestion and acceptance is attributable, because an audited document cannot contain unattributed changes
**No live cursors.** Presence says which component each person is in and their mode (COL-001, COL-002), not where their cursor is; cursor-level presence belongs to the co-editing COL-N01 rules out
**No deleting review history.** Not by its author, not by an author of the component, not by a tenant administrator (COL-049, COL-050). Resolution is how a thread stops mattering
**No queued or automatic application of a suggestion** (COL-043). A change to a document is made by a person, at a moment they chose, against the content in front of them
**Not an ETL tool.** Reshaping, joining and aggregating happen in the source or in the query, not in a pipeline this product owns
**No writing back to a source.** Every connection is read-only, and a connector that could write would make this product part of somebody's change-control boundary
**No ad-hoc queries written by document authors.** A query is a reviewed artifact; an author chooses one and supplies parameters
**No dashboards and no exploratory analysis.** Scope §8 is explicit, and a report is not a BI tool with prose around it

**No revising the source.** A revision (DAT-057) changes what this document says, never what the source system holds. DAT-N02 is why: a connection that could write back would put this product inside somebody else's change control

**No unmarked revision.** There is no way to make a hand-entered value look like a queried one wherever DAT-115 marks it - in the product and in a publication's provenance - and no setting that turns the marking off
**No uploaded file as a data source.** An upload is a push, and a push can never be checked for a source revision. A file is read from S3-compatible storage or over HTTP (DAT-074)
**No autonomous publishing.** Nothing a model produces reaches a reader without a person accepting it
**Not a model host.** The product calls endpoints; it does not serve models
**No training on customer content.** This product does not train on it. An endpoint that does may only be used where that is stated in configuration (GEN-031)

**No tool the product does not define.** The assistant's tools are the product's own capabilities and nothing else (GEN-007) - a rule about what it may **do**, never about what a user may **ask** (GEN-047, GEN-050)
**No shared personal prompt.** A personal prompt is private until somebody promotes it (GEN-055); there is no setting that shares one, and none that lets a template bind one
**No silent discard.** A generated proposal leaves the record only by somebody discarding it deliberately, and the fact that they did stays (GEN-040, GEN-041)
**Not an identity provider.** Authentication federates to the customer's provider, or to a Google account where the tenant has none. The product holds no password (IAM-042)
**No permission finer than a component.** A component is the unit of reuse and of review; permissions inside one would have to travel with it into every document that uses it

**No sharing between tenants.** An outsider participates as a guest principal inside the host tenant (section 11), never as a bridge between two. Cross-tenant sharing is deferred rather than refused - see [ADR-0011](../../decisions/0011-external-participation-guests-and-identified-links.md)
**No enforcement in the renderer.** The renderer is untrusted in both deliveries; what it hides is presentation, and the service refuses regardless
**No permission outside a role** (IAM-062). A grant binds a role to a principal or a group at a level; there is no per-user permission set beside it, because section 8 could not explain one
**No vendor account inside a tenant** once it is bootstrapped (IAM-061). Support reaches a tenant through access that tenant granted, bounded and can revoke (**ADM-023**), and by no other route
**No unattended import**, at any scale (IMP-003)
**No claim of lossless Word round-tripping** (IMP-025)
**No import that bypasses validation** (IMP-017)
**No migration service disguised as a feature.** Bulk conversion of a legacy estate is a project, and it is a person's job

**No scanning of body content for personal data.** Section 4's scope is the identities a document carries as metadata and annotations. A customer's name inside the prose of a report is content the customer wrote, and this product does not inspect, classify or redact it

**No unattended import _of a foreign document_** (IMP-003, IMP-N01). The product's own export format is not a foreign document: it is already components, needs no split judgement, and is importable (IMP-039)
**No ontology with inference** (LIB-027)
**No terminology as text macros.** A term is a reference; expansion is how one is inserted, not what one becomes (LIB-019)
**No boilerplate here.** A standard phrase or paragraph is reuse, and belongs to **REU** as a component or a variable
**Not a full termbase.** Concept-level modelling, term extraction and translation memory are separate products
**One definition per term.** A term carrying two senses is two terms. Concept-level modelling is the termbase LIB-N04 rules out, and a single definition slot is the deliberate consequence

**No mirror of an external source.** The product searches PubMed, Crossref and their like and keeps what a document cites (LIB-031, LIB-033). Ingesting a registry would be maintaining somebody else's database badly
**Not an electronic signature provider.** The product records an attested act; a qualified signature is somebody else's business
**No editing or deletion of audit entries**, by anybody, including an administrator
