Claims serialise on the component (`serialise`); one wins, the other is told at once, shown no editable surface, and keeps what it typed (component-editor.md's Claiming)

The holder's window hears `lock` with `taken`, or its next save is refused `lock_taken`; it names the taker, says their saved work is kept, and offers what it had not sent as text to copy; their iterations are theirs to recover when they hold the lock again
The take period, `lock_take_minutes`, 5 by default, is a tenant setting, and a value not shorter than the release period is refused
The holder is warned at the ask and given a declared grace of 60 seconds in which any saved work keeps the lock
A thread is anchored to a span of a component's text (its block and the text it quotes), a table cell (its first block), a whole component, or an outline node
`POST /v1/threads/{id}/resolution` records who and when; nothing else ends a thread
Comments in the order made, each with its author; replying is a comment on the thread
A comment names people as mentions; each who may read what the thread is on is told in their inbox, and one who may not is told nothing, which the composer is then told
An anchor is a block's identifier and the text it quotes, not a position: it holds through any change that keeps that block and that text
A thread whose block, node or quoted text is gone is listed **orphaned**, never dropped, with the text it was on

A deleted component holds no lock: a held one refuses the deletion. Deleting it removes every presence in it, which each stream hears as `presence_left`, as it hears a dropped connection (COL-004). A document that once placed it places it in no version now (DL-C): its threads are listed there **orphaned**, placed nowhere, to whoever may read it but for its deletion, and opening one says it was deleted

Starting and resolving a thread, sending a suggestion and accepting, rejecting or withdrawing one are said in a `role="status"` region there, empty, from the start, naming which and where: "Thread started on “the tray” in 1 Method.", "Ada's suggestion on 1 Install the printer accepted." Accept all and Reject all count rather than name: "Accepted 3 suggestions. 1 left pending, which could not be."

A thread's anchor has a border beneath its tint, a cell's a dashed outline; a redline underlines and strikes through, and says "Added" and "Removed"; suggestions and states are named in words. Under `forced-colors: active` the borders, lines and words stay, in the system's colours, and a state dot stays a dot
`GET /v1/documents/{id}/threads`: its own nodes' and every placed component's the caller may read, each placed against the version its occurrence resolves to, filtered by state, author and since when
Threads are their own tables: nothing a publish reads holds one
No route deletes a thread or a comment, and the runtime role holds no delete on either
Each thread records the version it was made against; comments, edits and resolutions are insert-only
An edit is a new text row; the comment shows the latest and says it was edited, and every earlier text is kept and readable to whoever reads the thread
Every time here is a `timestamptz`, sent as an instant, and shown in the reader's own time zone with its time
`notification`: one row per recipient, listed in the inbox newest first, unread marked
`notification_preference`: for each kind - mentions, replies on a thread one is in, resolutions - at once, in a daily digest, or never
The worker folds a person's held events, once a day, into one notification saying how many of what, and where, deciding again what they may read
A notification names its kind, who, and the thread and artifact by identifier: never the text. The inbox shows a title only to a reader of it, at the moment it is read

A thread is started internal, or made so while open by somebody inside, once (0109's `thread_internal`, audited `thread.made_internal`); to a principal from outside it does not exist - listed, read, replied to, resolved, counted on a round, told of, held in the inbox or found - and the page marks it **Internal** (the R13 plan, R13-C, R13-D)
The digest holds counts and identifiers alone, on the same terms

Kept 90 days, then swept; deleted by its recipient alone; a second copy of tenant content, in the tenant's schema and read only by its recipient (IAM-066). A deprovisioned principal's inbox is deleted with them - no act deprovisions anybody yet, so the rule is stated and waits for that act
The document view offers **Review** beside Reading and Authoring
Review shows threads and suggestions and lets the reader start and answer them, and suggest in a draft of their own; it never edits the content
Review is offered to whoever holds `comment` or `suggest` on the document, as Authoring is to whoever holds `edit` (IAM-080)

A reviewer suggests by editing a private draft of a component; the suggestion is that draft beside the content, drawn as a redline over the current version by the comparison's renderer, and the content is unchanged until it is accepted
A suggestion records its author and when it was made, and the version it was made against
Accepted or rejected one at a time, or in bulk: every pending suggestion on a component or across a document, optionally of one author
A component's pending suggestions are listed, and a document's across every component it places, `?state=pending`, as each reader may read them
One suggestion is one act: accepting applies every change it holds, or none of them
Accepting applies every change a suggestion proposes, in every block, as one act; rejecting ends the whole of it as one
Accepting records a version authored by whoever accepts, `suggestion.accepted` naming the suggestion and its author; rejecting and withdrawing are audited too
Suggestions are made, listed and drawn with no lock, while the component is held

Accepting or rejecting serialises on the component and holds it for its transaction where it is free, the automatic claim, ending with the act; where the caller holds the lock, refused `edits_pending` while they have saved work after the current version
Accepting or rejecting is refused `lock_held` while another holds the component's lock, naming the holder and when it is expected to release (COL-007); the suggestion stays pending
Nothing applies a suggestion but a person's accepting it, one or in bulk: no release, timeout or round applies one
Its author withdraws a pending suggestion; the withdrawal records who and when, and the suggestion is kept
A suggestion that no longer applies to the component as it is now is listed **stale**, with each place it no longer fits and why; it stays pending, never rejected on its author's behalf
A round names its reviewers, its scope - the document or nodes of it - and its due date ([Review rounds](#review-rounds))
Each reviewer is not started, in progress (**Start**, or a completion reopened) or complete, derived from their own acts
The round's summary: every reviewer by state and the count complete of all, to anybody who may read the round

A round may name a principal from outside who may comment on or suggest to the document and reads all it covers, on the terms an internal one is named on; what they may do is the cap's (IAM-047; the R13 plan, R13-B)
A round may name a baseline: its reviewers read and comment on the baseline's fixed page in Review mode, threads judged against the pins
A completion says **with comments** or **nothing to say**, each apart from not started
A reviewer reopens their completion while the round is open, recorded with who and when
Complete only from an explicit completion; nothing is read from silence or activity elsewhere
`compareContent` (content), `compareOutlines` (structure) and `compareResolved` (resolved output), in `packages/domain`
Resolved comparison names `overridden` for a node whose document's overrides differ, apart from `edited`: the component is the same, so it is never a fork

Any two versions of a component (`GET /v1/components/{id}/comparison?from&to`); any two baselines of a document, or a baseline and the document as it resolves now (`GET /v1/baselines/{id}/comparison?with`)
Matching precedes ordering: a unit matched in both is one change, `moved` and `edited` together where both hold
Identifier first; then, among blocks of one type left over, the highest Dice at or above 0.4, greedily, best first
Every change carries `matched: 'identity' \| 'similarity'`, and the redline draws a similarity match apart
The redline drawn over the newer side in the page, and exported as one self-contained HTML file **(default)**

`compareResolved` names, per node, each cause that holds: a component version, a dataset version, a definition version, the layout's or theme's version. Conditions are T4's: the identity until then, so never a cause yet
The same for two baselines under different template versions: a definition cause told from an edit, field by field
Every route reads as its caller. A component they may not read is its node alone: where it stands, never whether it changed; in the page and the export

Content and structure: two baselines of 300 components, 20 blocks each, and a component with 300 versions listed and compared, held to counted operations in CI and timed in the service **(default, provisional)**; resolved output budgeted apart
The editor's **Compare** lists the component's versions, who cut each and when, and draws the redline against the one chosen
Any two versions; revisions when LIF designates them, as `revision.version` already names them
**My changes**: the editor compares the version it opened from with what it holds now, in the browser, so it needs no lock and lags no save
The same view is the author's own changes, told apart from others' suggestions when phase 6 draws them
`GET /v1/changes?since=` for a document (its outline, the components it places and its values accepted), a space, or a listing's results by `listing.ts`, as the caller may read them
Versions are never deleted (VER-036), so the record begins where the artifact did, or where the environment was made; a `since` before it answers from there and says so
After a pause in changes the renderer sends the whole content and values as an iteration; there is no save action for drafts

The editor holds the `condition` mark, which excludes nothing, so several stand over one run and ranges overlap; **Condition** (Ctrl or Cmd, Alt and O) sets one over the selection from the declared axes and their values, replacing one on the same axis and keeping one on another ([the R6 plan](../plans/2026-10-16-r6-conditions-and-profiles.md), R6-H)
Conditional text is drawn tinted and underlined dashed, wherever the component's text is shown, with what it depends on as its title: _Only where audience is regulator_ (R6-H)

Where the selection is already conditioned on an axis, the Condition dialog says how to word it differently for other readers and offers **Add alternative**: a copy beside it, kept for the axis's other values, selected to rewrite (R6-H)

The renderer reports a change saved only when its iteration is acknowledged, and reopening after a closed tab, a crash or a lost connection says when the author last saved work no version holds and offers **Recover**, which lists it and every other retained iteration of theirs to restore
A save indicator with three states - saved, saving, not saved and retrying - with the time of the last acknowledged save; the change to not saved is announced
One `prosemirror-history` per component; the session's steps are kept in `sessionStorage` and replayed into a fresh history on reload, back to the version the session opened from

Cutting a version clears the history and the stored steps, and a reload that finds steps recorded against an older version discards them, so undo never reaches past the version the session opened from or one cut during it

Reaching back past the version the session opened from is not the session's: undo stops there (CNT-169), and an earlier version comes back only by **Restore** in the Versions panel, a separate act decided on `edit`, refused while anybody holds the lock, and audited `content.restored` ([storage-and-versioning.md](storage-and-versioning.md); the RS plan)
A version is cut by **Save version** or **Done editing** and by nothing else - not a keystroke, a timer, a lost connection or a timeout

Which component the cursor is in is the one open in its card, the others shown as read text. Whether the reader may edit each now is said before it opens: the texts route answers each readable occurrence's `mayEdit` and lock, decided and read as the component's own route decides and reads them, and a card says "You may read this component but not edit it." or who holds it and when they are expected back, in the reader's own time (`heldSentence`); the open editor's notice says the same

A component's text carries one class, `TEXT_CLASS`, wherever it is shown - the editing surface and a document's read text alike - and the editor's stylesheet sets all of that class's typography once - spaces kept as typed, no ligatures, the size, leading and every block's spacing - while its rules for the surface alone set only the caret, the selection and a placeholder. The read text is `renderContent`, the same schema's own rendering, so opening a component moves nothing

The surface's structure is the elements that say so: a list is `ul` or `ol` of `li`; a definition list is `dl > div > dt + dd`, each definition its own node rendered `dd` ([ADR-0026](../decisions/0026-a-definition-is-its-own-editor-node.md)); a table is a `table` of `th` and `td` in a `figure` captioned by its `figcaption`; and a footnote is a marker named _Footnote_ whose text opens in an editor named _Footnote text_. A document's read text renders the same schema, so it carries the same lists and tables

The session never promotes an iteration on its own; iterations are rows the storage design keeps immutable and timestamped, and read by their writer alone, only while holding the lock, through recovery (RC-A; VER-001 to VER-003). CNT-089, which it superseded, repeated those rows

A **Recovery** panel, opened by **Saved text** while editing or by **Recover**, lists the lock holder's own retained iterations of the component, newest first, and restores one - content and values together - after saving as an iteration anything on screen not yet saved
Every write in the session - iteration, version, release - carries the lock, and nothing here assumes the author is the only one who could write
The lock is claimed by the first change an author makes, to content or metadata, not by a separate act; changes wait for the claim rather than being refused
The lock gates writes to the component and nothing else: reading it, and later commenting and suggesting, never ask for it
**Done editing** releases the lock and cuts a version of what changed; a lock expiring cuts nothing
The lock is a row per component; nothing locks a document
The service checks the lock on every mutating component request and refuses one from anybody but the holder with `lock.held`, naming the holder and the expected release
Creating a component requires a component type, offered with the tenant's default preselected; the version row's type column is not nullable, and no iteration or version changes it

"Creating a component" takes a title, a base language and a base direction, in a space the author chose from those `GET /v1/spaces` says they may create in; the component exists at `0.1` from the moment it is created
A fixed field is read-only in the panel, naming the schema that fixes it, and the service refuses an iteration or a cut whose value for it differs from the default, naming field and schema
An insertion palette of mathematical, Greek, and scientific and technical symbols, as a keyboard-navigable grid that inserts characters, dimming those the typeface at the cursor lacks (W-M)
Every command is in a keymap and in the toolbar; the toolbar is a single tab stop with arrow-key movement, and `F6` moves between the regions of the view

Emphasis, strong, underline, subscript, superscript, inline code and a quoted phrase are each applied and removed from the toolbar and by a shortcut in the keymap ([What an author can do with each thing in the model](#what-an-author-can-do-with-each-thing-in-the-model)); nothing on the surface chooses a typeface, a size or a colour, and the model has no member to hold one (content-model.md, CNT-008)

An equation's alternative is generated from its MathML wherever a generator is available - when an equation is made or changed, in the component's language where the generator speaks it (publishing.md, EQ-D) - stored as `alttext`, and always editable
Equations render as native MathML carrying `alttext`, which assistive technology reads; an equation is reachable and opened by keyboard

An equation is made in every context the statement names - running text, a table's cell, a footnote and a caption on the surface, and a section's heading in the outline's title field - and publishing.md's equations 2 sets each in the PDF
The surface sets `spellcheck`, so the delivery's own checker marks spelling as the author types
A run carrying a language mark whose language differs from the component's base language is rendered with `spellcheck="false"`, so a passage in another language is never flagged

The web delivery uses the browser's checker; the desktop shell enables the base languages of the components open, through one platform bridge call, where the platform lets it, and on macOS, which chooses its own, the product says so; so neither lacks a checker
A language tag the content model takes and a publication cannot carry is named back to the author, in the dialog they typed it in, before the mark is applied; **OK anyway** then applies it

The browser suite's `accessibility.test.ts` (W13.2) runs axe-core over WCAG 2.2 AA's automatable criteria in every state of the editor and the document view a person reaches - the cursor in each block and mark, each dialog and each panel open, the title strip's fields, a save that failed, Reading and Authoring, the outline, the version chooser, the preview and the publishing panel - in the pinned Chromium against the whole stack, in CI's whole-system job on every push and pull request. A violation fails it unless the suite's allow-list holds it by rule, element and state, with the issue filed for it

Before each release a person audits the editor against WCAG 2.2 AA by [the audit guide](../guides/auditing-a-release.md): the criteria no automated check reaches, by keyboard and with a screen reader, in the states the suite checks, with what axe could not decide beside them. The record is committed as `docs/audits/<version>/wcag.md`, and the release's baseline verifies CNT-177 by `attestation`, naming who looked and when

By the two above together, and never by a test: a baseline declares CNT-078 `inherited` from `CNT-177, CNT-176`, and the gate meets a requirement inherited from several only when every one of them is included and met, so the editor is said to meet WCAG 2.2 AA only in a release whose suite passed and whose audit a person made. An attestation naming its record under `docs/audits/` is refused where the file is not there, and the guide refuses the audit while the suite's allow-list holds anything. No test title cites it
A tree of typed block nodes, JSON-serialised, validated in `packages/domain`. Read as same-family with the editor rather than object-identical - see "How CNT-001 is read"
`id` is required on every block, allocated at creation and unique within the component
A mark is a member of a set on a text node, never an element, so two marks cover overlapping ranges with nothing between them
`id` is required on every mark; an annotation fragmented across text nodes repeats one id

Excluding is the profile's (REU-021, R6-C): every run whose condition the profile does not select is excluded in one pass, so every fragment carrying one condition, in any run or block, goes together in one profile pass; a paragraph it empties goes with them (the R20 plan, R20-C)
The mark schema is a closed discriminated union. A new type is a schema version with a migration and a fixture, not a setting
No milestone, no range-start, no range-end, no standoff table. The overlap needs no construct because marks are sets
No node and no mark has a member for a typeface, a size, a colour or spacing. There is nowhere to put one
Resolution rewrites content and preserves `id` on every block it keeps
One parse entry point validates on creation, on change and on read-back. No other path constructs a document
`schemaVersion` is a member of the root, so content describes itself once it leaves the database. VER-010's column is derived from it at insert and the two must agree
A fixture directory per schema version, never deleted, and one test migrating every fixture to current
A failed read returns a named quarantine result identifying the artifact, the version and the failure. No path yields partial content
`title` is a member of the root
`title` and `language` are inside the versioned content, so they are inside `content_hash` and a version records what the component was called when it was cut
The root's members are closed - `schemaVersion`, `title`, `language`, `direction`, `content` - and a metadata value is never one of them. Adding a member is a schema version
`paragraph`, the default block

`list` carries `kind`: ordered, unordered or definition. A definition list's item also carries the `term` it defines, as inline content, so a term can be emphasised, linked or given its own language - see "A definition list reaches a reader as a list"
A list item holds block content, so a list nests by construction and six levels is a floor rather than a limit, in any mixture of kinds

An ordered list carries `start` and `format` - decimal, alphabetic or roman - local to that list and unrelated to the outline's numbering. `start` is an integer of 0 or more in the shape, and a start of 0 under a lettered or roman numbering is refused by the walk - see "Where a list's start number is held"
`table` declares header rows and header columns, carries cell spans, and carries a caption
`figure` carries an asset reference and a caption, and never asset bytes
`preformatted` holds text with whitespace significant and an optional language label
`blockquote` holds block content and an optional attribution, which may carry a citation inline
`equation` as a block
Alternative text is a three-state and absent is not one of them, so publishing cannot find it missing because it cannot be missing
There is no spacer construct, and validation refuses two adjacent empty paragraphs - see "What CNT-023 forbids, exactly"
Validation requires at least one block, and a newly created component is exactly one empty paragraph
A caption-bearing block carries the same required `id` as any other block, which is the identity the outline numbers by
Every block carries `id` whether or not it carries a caption, so any block can be a cross-reference target
A table cell holds inline content and `image` is an inline node, so an image in a cell needs no construct of its own
A figure and an inline image each carry `imageStyle`, a name drawn from the catalogue STY owns
Neither carries a width, a height or a unit of any kind. There is no member to hold one
`text` is the only leaf node, and marks apply to it
`equation` inline
`footnote` is an inline node placed at the span it annotates, carrying the note's content

`crossReference` carries an identifier of its own, a target identity - a closed union of a block of its own component, a block of another, or an outline node - and a display kind, and has no member for a number or a title
`citation` inline
`variable` carries a name and no value
`binding` carries a query reference and no value
Eight character marks: emphasis, strong, underline, subscript, superscript, inline code, defined term, quoted phrase
`condition` carries an axis and permitted values, present in the first schema version stored as CNT-116 requires
`suggestion` carries an operation and an author, present from the first schema version
`comment` carries a thread identity, present from the first schema version
The root carries a BCP 47 base language; a `language` mark carries a BCP 47 tag, validated on entry rather than on use
`underline` is in the set, and this document says plainly that it is the one mark named for its appearance
`image` is an inline node, so it sits inside a run of text
`hyperlink` is a mark rather than a node, so it overlaps a condition or a suggestion exactly as the others do
The scheme allowlist is enforced in validation and again in the pipeline's sanitise stage, so a target with another scheme is refused before it can be stored
A `footnote` inline node sits at the span it annotates
A cell holds inline content, so a cell-anchored note is the same construct as a span-anchored one
`table` carries an optional table-level note. It is not an inline anchor, because a table is not a span
A table may declare key columns. Where declared an anchor names the key value; where not, it names row and column and is marked as the weaker form

Footnote content is paragraphs, holding no table, no image and no footnote. The schema admits paragraphs alone, so a table is refused there; the image and the footnote are refused by the walk `parseContentDocument` runs, which a section title runs too. The `condition`, `language`, `comment` and `suggestion` marks, which the closed list does not name, are admitted in a footnote, because they annotate text rather than add content
MathML is the one stored representation, whatever the entry route
LaTeX entry converts to MathML at the boundary, the same discipline CNT-056 applies to Unicode. The LaTeX typed is kept beside it as a non-authoritative input record
`citation` carries an entry identity and has no text member, so typed citation text is not representable
The entry is an artifact in the space; a citation holds its identity and never a copy of it
`citation` carries an optional locator beside its reference
NFC is applied in the pipeline's normalise stage and asserted by validation, so no un-normalised string can be stored
Direction is explicit on the root and on any run that differs, never derived from the language tag - see "Why direction is not derived"
A Markdown reader feeds the same pipeline, through the HTML reader: every structure a component can hold is kept, a heading kept as a paragraph, and the report names what was rewritten or dropped

Word's paste is read from the HTML Word puts on the clipboard, by the HTML reader in `packages/readers`, not by an OOXML reader: its list paragraphs as lists, its tables, its emphasis, and each footnote as a footnote where its anchor stands, holding its note's paragraphs with their marks, read from Word's note list; a heading is kept as a paragraph, and a note that cannot be found or an anchor inside a note is left out and named in the report
An HTML reader feeds the same pipeline and keeps every structure a component can hold, definition lists included; a heading is kept as a paragraph, and the report names what was rewritten or dropped

Text is JSON strings, so every character but U+0000 is storable in running text - Postgres cannot hold U+0000 in `jsonb`, and the store refuses it - and read back in the NFC CNT-056 requires, the astral planes included. Preformatted text refuses the C0 controls but the tab and the line feed, U+007F and the C1 controls, and the line and paragraph separators, each invisible or a second spelling of a line break (`forbiddenInPreformatted`). The editor holds and shows it through the same mapping and saves what is typed among it whole. A publish judges each character a whole code point at a time and refuses one no face can set as `glyph_missing`, naming it, for the PDF and Word alike, since `assemble` serves both (STY-049's check)
The report is a collector threaded through all six stages, returned with the admitted content rather than logged
A stage that discards or rewrites must append to the report; the verification rule below requires every admission test to assert the report as well as the output
The normalise stage drops typeface, size and colour, and there is no member in the model for any of them to survive into
The sanitise stage runs before normalise, so scripts, event handlers, embedded objects and disallowed link targets are gone before anything else touches the content
Each dropped or rewritten hyperlink is a report entry of its own, naming the target it had
The re-identify stage allocates a new `id` for every block, so copying cannot duplicate an identifier
The re-identify stage drops annotations whose owning artifact does not travel, and appends one report entry each
The migrate stage runs before validate: content at an earlier schema version is brought to current or refused with a named error, and is never stored unmigrated
One pipeline serves a foreign paste and an internal copy, so the report is to one standard because it is one implementation
The defined-term mark carries a term identity and has no text member, so a term cannot be typed as text
A component declares a base language and any run may declare its own, so a language variant is a component in its own right rather than a shape the model has to gain later
Structure, marks, references, bindings and terms are nodes and members rather than text, so a round-trip has nothing to lose and nothing translatable to mistake them for

A message form is a node, its arms the plural categories of CLDR 48.2.0 compiled into the domain and held to the interface's FormatJS by a parity test; the publish and the editor select by one function (`armFor`), and a translator fills the target language's arms. Gender is a named gap below
A figure's alternative text may be inherited, which is the state that reads the asset's default
A figure's own text is one of the three states, and it overrides the asset's default
Decorative is a state of its own rather than an empty string, so no alternative text is a declaration rather than an omission
Inherited alternative text carries the asset's language; a figure's own text takes the language of the component holding it
Administration → CT Studio connects a space, first or later, without the API
The hand-off page gives CT Studio's `.env` entry and steps, with the token shown once and no key
A property is mapped, ignored, or unlisted; an unlisted one is reported and listed for the space
Each space's row disconnects it: its grant and settings go, its deliveries, the token and other spaces stay
The bridge contract served under `/bridge`, signed, acting as a service identity; ADR-0071 carves it out
The published conformance suite run in process in the service's tests, and against a running stack
Images checked first, then everything in one tenant transaction; a refusal or failure writes nothing
`bridge_delivery` keyed by the delivery key; a replay answers the stored first receipt
`update.expected` checked against the latest versions under each artifact's lock; any difference refuses all
Identifiers derived from the document's persistent id and CT Studio's own element ids, the same every delivery
Each version's note and `bridge_delivery` record the source, its hash, the decomposer and the user delivered for
Data rows in a delivery store's tenant schema, read through a `connection` and SQL query definitions
What could not be carried listed in the receipt and the delivery record, never dropped silently
`connection` is an artifact kind in one space of one tenant's schema; its version carries a `name` and the settings of one source ([The connection](#the-connection))

A connection's `type` is `postgres`, `sqlServer` (deferred, [ADR-0038](../decisions/0038-sql-server-is-deferred-past-the-first-release.md)), `http` or `s3`, and a query definition's fetch reads CSV, XLSX, JSON or JSON Lines from an S3 object or an HTTP response; every one is pulled by the connector
The credential is sealed into `connection_credential` in the tenant's schema, with a key only the connector holds; no route answers it, so it is write-only from every client
`GET /v1/connections/{id}` answers `credential: { set, setBy, setAt }` from the latest credential row, and nothing a route answers carries the sealed value or the secret

The secret is opened only in the connector's per-request child, goes in a header never a URL, and is kept out of every log, telemetry event, export, crash report and error; the spike's case 2 matrix becomes a test for each path, in the service and in the connector

`test` answers `ok`, or `connection_failed` alike for a refused or filtered port, an unknown host, a guarded address and a wrong credential, naming no address and echoing no credential; checks of the authenticated account are reported after it by name ([The connection test](#the-connection-test))

`identity` is `service`, or `endUser` by `asserted` where the connector declares it (DAT-078); an asserted act runs as the caller, by the sign-in attribute the connection names, and one whose caller it cannot name is refused, `identity_unavailable`, before anything runs (D7)

`endUser` by `delegated`: a delegated act needs the provider access token a session through the tenant's own provider holds, so a Google-route session or a personal API token is refused, `identity_unavailable`. Designed here and not built: T7's, by [ADR-0041](../decisions/0041-the-delegated-provider-token-is-deferred-past-the-first-release.md) and [ADR-0044](../decisions/0044-the-delegated-tokens-requirement-moves-past-the-first-release.md)

Each connection type's connector declares the mechanisms it supports - `postgres` and `sqlServer` (once built, ADR-0038) asserted, `http` delegated, `s3` none - and a connection version declaring another is refused, `identity_not_supported`

Where a connection is used - the definitions naming it and, through their bindings and resolutions, the documents - is computed when asked, `GET /v1/connections/{id}/uses`, and the retire screen shows it before it proceeds

Nothing deletes a connection; retiring one is refused, `connection_in_use`, naming each definition that is not itself retired and names it, so no definition is left pointing at nothing and nothing cascades

Setting a credential inserts a row and cuts no version, so no stored result or resolution changes; the service tests the connection at once and, on a failure, reports it once, naming every definition that names the connection
The connector holds no platform credential and has no route to the platform; each request runs in a fresh process handed one opened credential, which exits with the request

Under asserted identity the account is checked at every run, describe and sample, in the transaction before the assertion, and refused, `account_holds_privilege`, if it may `SELECT` any relation or column outside the catalogues by grant, ownership, `PUBLIC`, `pg_read_all_data` or an inherited role, or is a superuser; the test reports the same finding (the D7 plan, D7-D)

On PostgreSQL an asserted identity runs only builder-generated text, the SQL fallback refused; on SQL Server, once built (ADR-0038), the assertion is a `read_only` `SESSION_CONTEXT` key or `EXECUTE AS USER ... WITH COOKIE` with the cookie held by the connector
No source connection is reused: the child process that opened it closes it and exits with its one request, so a connection that carried a user's identity is always discarded

Within two seconds of a sign-out or a token's revocation committing, every connector call of that session or token is closed and its child killed, the source losing the query within 250 ms; the act answers `authority_ended` naming why, logged, recording nothing; the session's event stream closes (the D7 plan, D7-I)
`queryDefinition` is an artifact kind in one space whose version carries a `title` and exactly one `connection`, a connection artifact's identifier
A definition is an artifact under the same grants as content - read to read it, edit to make or change it - and every change is a version, `content.version_cut` on the log

A query definition versions through `artifact_version` by `recordVersion`, with an author, `schemaVersion`, the digest and the insert-only grant every artifact has; a change is a new version from `openedFrom`
`queryDefinition` is a search kind, its entry written with each version from its title, description and column names
Each parameter declares `name`, `type` from the column vocabulary but `image`, `required`, `list`, and `permitted` values as a list or a range
A variation is a parameter whose permitted values are the keys of fragments the definition declares; its value selects one as an own property and is never placed in the query
Every value is checked against its declaration before the connector is asked, and a value that fails refuses the act, `parameter_invalid`, naming the parameter, the rule and the value

A database value is the driver's bound parameter; an HTTP value is placed by a builder that encodes it for its position and refuses what that position cannot carry; a file's is a typed filter over canonical rows. No path splices a value into text

Sources, columns, joins and conditions are the definition's own structure or text; a parameter supplies a value or, as a variation, selects among declared fragments, so no parameter changes a query's shape
The connector's suite runs the spike's case 5 values - 3,792 hostile and ill-typed - through every parameter type and every binder, and each is refused by name or bound inert
A database definition's fetch is `builder`, a saved query tree, unless it is `sql`; the connector generates the dialect's SQL from the tree at each run, and provenance keeps what ran
The tree's format, version 1, admits several sources, joins, nested queries as sources, grouping and aggregates from the start, though T2's screens offer one source

A text `contains` or `startsWith` carries `ignoreCase: true` where Match case is unticked, as it is on a new filter; absent, it matches case, as every comparison stored before it does. Both sides are lower-cased under ICU's root collation, a file's by `toLowerCase()`, alike (the MC plan)
Saving a definition whose fetch is `sql` needs `write_sql`, a permission of its own decided at the connection it names
A `sql` fetch is refused, `sql_not_permitted`, on a PostgreSQL connection whose identity is asserted, when saved and when run

The connection test checks, where the source can say - PostgreSQL's catalogues, and SQL Server's once built (ADR-0038) - that the account holds no write privilege, and a `sql` fetch is refused on a connection whose last test did not find it read-only
An `http` fetch is a request template - method, path segments, query, headers and a JSON body, each part fixed or a parameter - with the format and, for JSON, a pointer to the rows

JSON is read at a JSON Pointer to an array of objects or as JSON Lines; each column maps by a pointer relative to the row; a number is read from its source text; a nested value is refused, `nested_value`, unless its column is text

A column's type is one of `text`, `integer`, `decimal` with precision and scale, `date`, `time`, `localDateTime`, `instant` with a fractional precision, `boolean` or `image`; a value not exact in its type is refused by name, never rounded
The columns are the second step: proposed from `describe` for the builder and SQL, from the sample for HTTP and files, and saved only as the author confirms each
The connector checks every run against the declared columns and order and refuses, `result_mismatch`, a result that does not fit, never adjusting it
A definition's `order` is a total order that includes every key column, or `multiset`; the connector hashes the rows in that order or sorted by their canonical text
A definition declares `empty: 'valid'` or `'invalid'`, and a run of no rows against `invalid` fails, `empty_result`
A definition declares rows, bytes and seconds; a tenant setting lowers each, and a run takes the lesser

The tenant's runs at once, 4 unless an administrator lowers it and never past 16, across samples, resolves, checks and creations; one past it waits five seconds for a slot, then fails `query_throttled`, retryable and never partial ([Limits and cost](#limits-and-cost))

Every run is recorded - act, who, connection, query definition, document, time, rows, bytes, outcome - and totalled by query and by document for an administrator, and given whole as CSV ([Limits and cost](#limits-and-cost))

The connector's deadline covers the whole execution, and a limit reached cancels at the source: a PostgreSQL cancel request, a SQL Server attention once built (ADR-0038), an aborted HTTP or S3 exchange
Bytes are counted as they arrive, so a single value past the byte limit fails the execution, `byte_limit`
Reaching the row, byte or time limit is `row_limit`, `byte_limit` or `timeout`, and nothing is stored
A result cut by a limit is a failure and is never stored, so nothing can publish it as complete

Where an S3 object or an HTTP response states a length, a digest or a row count apart from its framing, the connector checks what arrived against it and refuses, `result_incomplete`, what does not match

An `image` column declares `base64` or `binary`; the connector admits only a PNG or a JPEG by the asset door's header reading, the cell is the stored hash, and `ingest` decodes it before the dataset version is recorded
`POST /v1/connections/{id}/sample` runs a draft definition with sample parameters, shows the result and its proposed columns, and stores nothing - so it runs before anything depends on the definition
Every change to a definition is a version, and a binding names its definition with an optional `version`: present pins it, absent floats at latest
Where a definition is used - the bindings naming it and the documents resolving them - is computed when asked, and the definition's editor shows it before a version is saved
`use_connection`, decided at the connection, is needed to run anything against it; reading a document that holds its results needs only `read` on the document

A query runs at the source as the identity its connection declares, so the source's own rules decide the rows - for an asserted identity, where the source's function, view and policy authors are trusted ([ADR-0040](../decisions/0040-asserted-identity-trusts-the-sources-function-authors.md)); an `s3` connection's identity may only be `service`

A stored result is read only through a document that resolves to it, on `read` on that document; fetching one - a resolve or a check - and accepting one each ask what the source side asks: `read` on the query definition it ran and `use_connection` on its connection, an accept on top of `edit` on the document ([Accept](#accept))
`dataset` is an artifact kind; each recorded result is an immutable version of it, named by an insert-only `dataset_name`, and a resolution names exactly one dataset version
Every binding a document resolves, checked or pinned, is resolved to a dataset version, whose content is its provenance record

A dataset version's content records the definition and connection with their versions, the canonical parameters, the SQL or request that ran, the identity, the time, the row count, `canonical: 1`, and the SHA-256 checksum; its own identifier is the dataset version
A dataset version is an `artifact_version`, insert-only, which a baseline pins as it pins any version; its rows are an object nothing sweeps while anything names it
Accepting adds a resolution row for that document's binding alone; another document holding the same dataset keeps its row, and its version, until somebody accepts there

A query definition's fetch may be `dataset`: the builder's tree over one stored result, run in the service from the result's stored rows, never the source; `read` on the dataset governs listing, sampling and resolving one ([A dataset as a source](#a-dataset-as-a-source))
A check compares a fresh result with the one held only where the opener's identity key is the dataset's; a different checksum is recorded as a dataset version and answered as a waiting revision

HTTP, S3 and PostgreSQL declare a `revision` capability; a run captures the source's revision (an ETag or Last-Modified, a version id or ETag, a revision statement's value) and a check asks it first, running nothing where it is unchanged ([Check](#check))
Accepting is its own route, and its resolution row names the version the binding held, the version it holds after, who and when
Only the service calls the connector, only from a route a person calls - resolve, check, a sample run, describe and test - and neither the worker nor a publish nor a preview has a route to it
Each act succeeds whole or fails by one named failure identifying the definition and, where the act has them, the binding and the document; a failed act records nothing
Every failure carries `attribution`: `connector`, `query` or `product`, fixed per code ([Failures](#failures))
A binding names its definition in `query`, its `parameters`, and, inline, `take`, the value it takes
A binding's parameter is `{ literal }` or `{ document }`, a document parameter by name, read from the document's parameter set when the binding is resolved
An inline binding's `take` is `{ column }`, of a result of exactly one row, or `{ key, column }`; the schema admits nothing else, so a binding identifying neither is refused when it is written

A field, a schema and a component type are each made at 0.1 by `createArtifact` and changed only by `recordVersion` from the version the caller opened; no route changes a stored version, and the chain's grant refuses it anyway

A variable is a definition of the environment's, `variable`: a key a content `variable` node names, a value type, its sources and its forms, chosen from the definitions rather than typed; its field source must be a field and its key no other variable's ([the R5 plan](../plans/2026-10-15-r5-variables.md))

A condition axis is a definition of the environment's, `conditionAxis`: a key a condition mark names and its permitted values, a closed list each with a key and a label, managed as fields are; its key is fixed once made and no other axis's ([the R6 plan](../plans/2026-10-16-r6-conditions-and-profiles.md), R6-A). Drawing its values from a vocabulary (LIB-022) is [vocabularies.md](vocabularies.md)'s

`definition_name` holds one row per definition: its kind and its name folded for comparison, unique per kind; making one and renaming one write it in the same transaction, and a name taken is refused, `definition_name_taken`, naming the definition that holds it

A component type's version is refused where two schemas it assigns disagree about a field's default, `assignment_conflict`, naming the field and both schemas, by `checkAssignment`; a template's is refused the same way already, by `resolveTemplate`'s `conflict` ([templates.md](templates.md))

An assignment names a schema and never a version of it, so it always takes the latest. A schema's next version is refused where its default for a field would differ from that of a schema applied beside it at any place - every component type and every template level assigning both, at their latest versions - `schema_conflict`, naming the field, the other schema and every such place

A field's next version is refused where it would make any schema's default for it invalid - every schema grouping the field, at its latest version, checked by `checkSchema` against the candidate field - `field_breaks_default`, naming the field, each schema and its default

The metadata panel beside a component, and the fields of a document and of the selected section on the document's page, run `validate` on every change against the fields that apply there, each failure shown beside its field and announced, and none of it blocks a save

A publication request validates every component version it resolves against the definition versions that version recorded (MET-017), and each failure is recorded against its node as the request's own, `component_metadata_invalid`, so the publication fails naming the component and the field. Cutting a version validates nothing

The text is one canvas on the theme's paper: every heading, a section's and a component's, set in the theme's heading role for its depth, and each component's text beneath its heading, with no card around it ([One scroll](#one-scroll))

A component's edges and its label appear when the pointer or the focus is in it, and for all of them while **Show boundaries** is on, and never otherwise ([Boundaries](#boundaries)). The one component open in an editor keeps its edges while it is open: that is the editor an author opened and closes with Done, not chrome the page puts round a component whatever the reader does
The page is in **Reading** or **Authoring**, said by a switch in its header that shows the mode it is in ([Modes](#modes))
Authoring is offered only where the document's `mayEdit` or an occurrence's allows it, and Reading otherwise, so a mode the permissions do not give is never offered ([Modes](#modes))
Authoring is offered where the reader may restructure the document or edit any component it places; anyone in Authoring may switch to Reading, and the page keeps that choice

Reading offers moving through the document and nothing that changes it; Authoring offers the outline's acts and each component's editor in place. The Publishing panel shows in both, to whoever may publish: publishing changes nothing in the document, and is the `publish` decision's rather than an editing affordance (DV-D, Ken's to overrule)
A component's label names the version its reference resolves to and whether it is the latest or pinned ([Versions](#versions))

A reference pinned below a newer version the reader may read says so beside its text, naming both, and offers **Compare**: the component's comparison (CNT-111) between them, asked for only then ([Versions](#versions))

In Authoring, where the reader may restructure the document, the label's version opens a list of the component's versions and **Always the latest**; choosing one is the outline's `set` of the reference's mode

A field definition carries `id`, `name`, `dataType` and `validation`; schemas refer to a field by `id`, so a field grouped by two schemas is one definition
`dataType` is a closed enum - `text`, `number`, `date`, `time`, `dateTime`, `boolean`, `user` - and `multiplicity` is `one` or `many`. Adding a type is a definition-schema version with a migration
A `dateTime` value must parse as ISO 8601 with an explicit offset or `Z`; a `date` or `time` value with an offset is refused
A `many` field's value is an array with no duplicate after normalisation, in the order given; `required` means at least one element; a default is an array; `maxValues` is optional
`checkValue(field, value)` takes the field and the value and nothing else, so no context can make a value valid in one place and invalid in another
A schema definition carries `id`, `name` and its entries, and is an artifact kind versioned by the one mechanism (ADR-0024)
Each schema entry is `{ field, required, default?, fixed }`
Resolution keys effective fields by field `id`, so a field reached through several schemas appears once, required if any entry or assignment requires it

A component type's assignment is `{ schema, requires: fieldId[] }`. There is no member that could loosen a field, change a default or fix a value, so an assignment cannot do those by construction. `requires` can only name a field the assigned schema groups, and a field becomes effective only through a schema entry, so `requires` cannot add one
A component type definition carries `id`, `name` and zero or more assignments, and nothing about content
`resolveComponentFields` takes a component type and its definitions and nothing about any document, so there is no input through which a document could contribute a field

Every environment is provisioned with a default component type - _Topic_, assigning no schemas - declared in `component_type_default` ([storage-and-versioning.md](storage-and-versioning.md)), which creating a component takes where its author names no type
`validate` takes the definition versions it is given; checking a stored version passes the versions recorded in `version_definition`, never the current ones
`definitionsFor(type)` names the current version of the type, each schema it assigns and each field those group; the service stamps that list on a version at promotion

`carryForward(values, effective)` returns the values whose field still applies, unchanged, and a `notCarried` list of every other value by field, which the version records. It fills only a field with no member, so it never changes a value that is present

Every failure is `{ code, field, rule, schemas, detail }`, with a stable `code`; the caller adds the artifact. A rule a schema imposed - required, fixed - lists every schema that imposed it, since more than one can. A requirement an assignment imposed names the schema assigned

`checkUserValues` checks that every `user` value names a principal of this tenant, over a tenant-scoped lookup of its directory, and the service runs it on every iteration it accepts and refuses on a failure, `metadata.user` ([User values](#user-values))

HTML is a third output from the same published document, one self-contained file to read on a screen, held to WCAG 2.2 AA in pinned Chromium (axe, reflow at 320 px and 200% text, every passage's language and direction), as the PDF is to PDF/UA-1 ([HTML](#html))

An index is set where the layout places one (`matter.index`), from the markers the published document carries after conditions and profiles: sorted by the document language's collation, a term's locators before its sub-entries, "see" and "see also" in the layout's words; page numbers in the PDF, fields Word fills in Word, section links in HTML ([The index](#the-index))

An index entry is marked in a component's text by an `indexMarker`, an inline atom of a term, an optional sub-entry, and a "see" or "see also"s, printing nothing where it stands ([The index](#the-index))

A publication is shared outside the organisation only with a named address: somebody from outside who signed in with it, verified, or the address invited as such; never one of the organisation's own, and nothing reads without a sign-in ([Shares](#shares))

A share expires at the tenant's default for access from outside, or earlier, within its cap; revoking removes its grant, and since somebody from outside is given no signed link, their next request for the publication or its bytes finds nothing ([Shares](#shares))
A publication says it is superseded where its document was published again later, under the same profile, from a later version, naming the newer only to whoever may read it ([Shares](#shares))
Each opening of a shared publication or fetch of its bytes by somebody from outside is audited `publication.shared_accessed`, and listed with their share to whoever may share it ([Shares](#shares))

A share is a grant of the fixed **Shared reader** role at that publication alone, time-bounded as every grant to somebody from outside is, in the external-access listing; nothing it reaches lists the organisation's people or spaces ([Shares](#shares))

A person's baseline still publishes a draft, and the live document only ever does
A variable that names no declared key, or resolves to nothing its type prints, fails the publish `variable_unresolved`, naming node, block and key; it is never printed as its name or as nothing
A variable's definition declares `forms` by context, laid over the document's formats: its title form in a section's title, its text form in a component's text
A variable resolves from the referring document's parameter set, its metadata, or a column of the one-row result it holds for the variable's query definition (the R10 plan, R10-B)

A publish or a preview may name a profile in place of the document's; the request and its publication record the profile it was made under, which 0106's rule holds equal (R6-F)
Conditions run before references resolve, so a reference to a paragraph its conditions take out fails `cross_reference_excluded` (R6-D; the R11 plan, R11-D)
Conditions are evaluated over each occurrence's content as the referring document places it, in that document's profile (R6-D)
Content conditioned on an axis the profile does not name fails the publish `axis_unset`, naming node, block and axis, unless the document's profile records `excludeUnset` (R6-E)

`selectOutline` takes out a section or a reference the profile does not select, with its subtree, before anything reads an occurrence; what it and a text condition take out is never counted, so it takes no number (the R11 plan, R11-C), as is a table, a bound table, a figure or a block equation its own conditions take out (R11-B)
A reference whose target a condition took out, a node, a block or a component block, fails the publish `cross_reference_excluded`, naming the reference and its target, never printed (R11-D)
The contents and the lists are generated from the selected outline and the conditioned content alone, so they hold only what the resolved document does
`order.test.ts` places transclusion first: before it, nothing is counted, a reference finds no table and a list holds none
`order.test.ts` places conditions before numbering, references and lists: composed after each, the section a profile takes out is numbered, found and listed
`order.test.ts` places variables before references, numbering and lists: composed after each, a caption's variable reaches neither the reference nor the list

Before any output is stored, each one's text and metadata (a PDF's pages, information and XMP; every XML part of a Word document) are searched for each four words of a passage its conditions took out that the kept text does not hold; a match fails the publish `condition_leaked`, naming the format, and nothing is stored (the R6 plan, R6-G). The order is stated under [The order](#the-order): resolve occurrences, conditions over content, contributions, number, references, generated matter, checks, projection. `order.test.ts` tests each adjacent pair: swapped where the code lets a test swap them, the output differing; refused at compile time where the types forbid it; and, where `assemble` runs the last stages in its own order - after the Word numbering check, the checks of the title, the language, a preview's words and the layout's words, then the references, one walk that checks and projects each block, then the contents, the check for something to publish, which reads it, and the lists - that check shown reading generation's answer, and a projection returned only where every check passed

A preview reads the document's latest version and each occurrence's current resolution, and says **Preview - not approved** on every page and once, as its sentence, at the start of the tagged text, in the layout's words ([Preview](#preview), PV-D)

A preview is a request of kind `preview` run by the publish job, the same `assemble`, template and engine; the differences are listed under [Preview](#preview) and none of them is in what the pages show but the notice

**Preview** on the document page asks for a preview of the version the page holds and opens it in a pane beside the text, the PDF in the browser's own viewer, so an author sees the pages without leaving the text or an editor open in it (PV-G)

A publication is always compiled with `--pdf-standard ua-1`; the publication path has no page-range parameter to pass, and Typst refuses `--pages` with `ua-1`. T1's preview is the whole document, tagged; only the warm range preview, T3's, omits tagging, and it is images, never a PDF
The compile root holds `data.json`, the template, the fonts and the assets, nothing else. The template reads values with `json()` and has no `eval`; content reaches Typst only as strings and numbers

A range preview's pages are images whose alternative text says each is an untagged preview page and names the tagged PDF; the panel says the same on screen and offers the tagged PDF beside it. T4's since ADR-0045

A warm compile, `typst watch` over the document's own root, and a clean compile of the same input make the same bytes - every PNG page, and the tagged PDF with the creation time pinned as every compile pins it ([The warm range preview](#the-warm-range-preview))

A save the editing session records is reflected in the range preview's pages within three seconds at the 95th percentile of twenty, none above six, on the 300-page reference document, measured on CI's runner from the save's commit to its pages recorded, each save reflowing the pages after it, and recorded beside the machine. The page's follow of it - asked every 150 ms - and its reading the pictures are not in the measure ([The warm range preview](#the-warm-range-preview))
A layout's paged format declares page size, orientation, margins as top, bottom, inside and outside, and a gutter

Running heads and feet are three slots each, holding literal words and the fields `title`, `section`, `page`, `pages` and `revision`; `revision` is the document version as `revision.version` (VER-009)

Page numbering is declared per matter - front, body, appendix - each with a format and whether it restarts; front matter is the generated front matter and the outline's `front` matter ([The layout](#the-layout))
A layout carries a numbering scheme in structure.md's shape; `number` is given the layout's, in the publisher, in the numbering route and in the outline panel

A layout holds one member per format, each its own declaration, so everything a page means is the `pdf` member's and nothing above it. Whether a format has pages is the format's kind (`PAGED`: the PDF and Word, never HTML), never stored (decision B of the second slice; the HT plan, HT-D): the shape lets a layout differ per format, and the Word slice is what cites it
A layout is an artifact kind versioned by the chain; a publication pins the layout version it used, and a baseline pins it as it pins any version (VER-018)
A format is supported where the layout has a member for it; a request naming another is refused `format_unsupported` before anything is queued

A layout's `language` is a BCP 47 tag, taken as a language range and matched to the document's language by RFC 4647 basic filtering (the second publishing plan's decision G): `en` takes `en-GB`. A document outside it is refused `layout_language` at the request, naming both tags, before anything is queued
A footnote is set as a Typst footnote at its anchor; a cell-anchored footnote sits in its cell, a table-anchored one at the caption. The regression corpus holds the spike's footnote cases
Headings come from outline nodes alone and are bookmarked, so the PDF's bookmarks are the outline with its numbers

A cross-reference in a paragraph's text - running text, a list's item, a quotation, a table's body cell, a footnote's text - is an internal link to its target, and one in a caption, a title, a term, an attribution, a table's note or a header row is text (structure.md, XR-D). Built by cross-references 2 and read back from the PDF

A header row is one `table.header` and a header column's cells are `pdf.header-cell(scope: "row")` under `--features a11y-extras`, each a `TH` whose scope veraPDF checks - measured under [Tables](#tables)

Compose resolves each figure's alternative text - its own, decorative, or inherited from the asset version's default - and a figure with none fails `alternative_missing`, naming the occurrence and block

Blocks are published in the document's order and tagged in it. Two things are drawn elsewhere, and each is tagged where the document has it: a figure its style floats, drawn at the head or the foot of its page, is read between the blocks either side of it, and in Word its text box is anchored in a paragraph of its own at the same place; a footnote, drawn at the foot of its page, is read inside the paragraph it stands in, where its anchor is. In Word a footnote is Word's own, and where Word reads it is Word's. That a table's header repeated on a later page is not read again is TAB-050's. Measured (W1.3)

The published document carries the document's language, each occurrence's base language where it differs and each `language` mark; the template sets `text(lang)` for each, and the Word writer sets `w:lang` ([word-output.md](word-output.md))

Each run carries its passage's language to the engine - a component's own, a language mark's - and in Word it is the run's `w:lang`, which Word hyphenates by where the document asks it to. Typst hyphenates by it, and a language it has no patterns for is not hyphenated at all, never as the document's. It breaks lines by it too: Croatian, Czech, Polish, Portuguese, Slovak and Spanish repeat a hyphen already in the text at the start of the next line, and CJK breaks by its own rules, which no pinned face sets; STY-085 asks the default theme for CJK. Otherwise the lines were the same in every language probed - English, French, German, Welsh, Turkish, Greek, Russian, Ukrainian, Serbian and Hebrew, with the pinned faces, compared line by line at 52 measures. Measured on Typst 0.15.1 over Latin text: patterns for Afrikaans, Albanian, Catalan, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Hungarian, Icelandic, Italian, Kurdish, Latin, Lithuanian, Norwegian (`no`, `nb`, `nn`), Polish, Portuguese, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish and Turkmen; none for Basque, Breton, Esperanto, Frisian, Galician, Indonesian, Irish, Latvian, Luxembourgish, Malay, Maltese, Northern Sami, Occitan, Romanian, Scottish Gaelic, Swahili, Vietnamese or Welsh. Patterns for scripts other than Latin were not probed (W1.3)

veraPDF checks every PDF in the worker against its PDF/UA-1 profile, after the publication is recorded (ADR-0030), by a `check_pdf` job queued in the transaction that records it, and queued again by the worker's sweep where it gave up; its report is retained whole - veraPDF's JSON, as it wrote it, in the tenant's store by its hash, as the PDF is - and summarised beside the publication in `publication_check`, one row per PDF output, insert-only: veraPDF's version, the profile, compliant or not, each rule failed with veraPDF's words for it, and the report's key, digest and size. Its page shows the summary and offers the report to download (W14.1)

Each clause, and how it is met. **Tagged**: every PDF is compiled by the pinned Typst to PDF/UA-1, `--pdf-standard ua-1` under `--features a11y-extras`, which tags it. **Checked on every publication**: `recordPublication` queues a `check_pdf` in the transaction that records a publication with a PDF, and the job checks the PDF against veraPDF's PDF/UA-1 profile and keeps its whole report beside the publication (PUB-091; queued again by the sweep where it gave up). **Passes**: held by the template and the regression corpus, not by a refusal - the corpus compiles the template's output through veraPDF on every change to the template or the engine, the six-level case passing with `H1` to `H6` tagged, and the budget's 311-page reference document passes every time it is checked. What the corpus shows the engine cannot tag, `assemble` refuses before anything is made: every node is a heading at its depth, a section's title or a component's, and the pinned Typst tags one below the sixth level as a paragraph, which veraPDF passes (measured, the regression corpus), so `assemble` refuses each node nested deeper than six levels where a PDF is asked for under a layout, `heading_too_deep`, naming it, and Word, which numbers and tags nine, publishes it (ADR-0031, W-E). A request made before layouts keeps saying what it always said, as its other refusals do, and is not refused so. The page's words offer Word alone only to a publish under a layout with a Word page: a preview is always a PDF, and a layout with no Word page makes none. **A publication that fails is shown, never hidden**: the check follows the record (ADR-0030), so a PDF veraPDF fails is not refused; it stays recorded, and its page says it failed and names each rule, as it says one that could not be checked. A failure found after recording is a defect in the template or the engine, which a case in the corpus then holds

Before each release a person reviews the Matterhorn Protocol checkpoints only a person can judge on the regression corpus (PUB-087) by [the audit guide](../guides/auditing-a-release.md): the corpus keeps every PDF it compiles where `ALLOY_CORPUS_PDFS` names a directory, each named by its case, and each checkpoint's human failure conditions are judged on those PDFs in a reader that shows the tag tree and with a screen reader. The record is committed as `docs/audits/<version>/matterhorn.md`, naming the protocol's version and each checkpoint's verdict, and the release's baseline verifies PUB-105 by `attestation`, naming who looked and when. A change to the engine, the template or the pipeline merged between two releases is reviewed with the release that ships it, and the record says which changes it reviewed

The reference document is declared in `apps/worker/src/publishing-budget.test.ts`: 30 chapters, each placing a component of 100 blocks - 150 each of figures, tables, numbered equations and footnotes, and 2,400 paragraphs of prose - set to 311 pages. It is published eleven times from `requestPublication` to the publication `processNext` records, the first reported and held to the maximum and the other ten held to a p95 of ten seconds and a maximum of thirty on a developer's machine, stated against [the reference configuration](../testing.md#the-reference-configuration) that `docs/testing.md` declares, and not run on CI, whose runner binds nothing (W-D), with the configuration and the document's pages and parts written beside the result in `.trace-results/worker.json`. CI leaves the test out, since a shared runner's speed is not the reference configuration. The measured span runs from `requestPublication` to the recorded publication, in process: it leaves out the HTTP route that asks for the publish and the time a request waits in the queue for a worker. The conformance report joins the publication after it is recorded, as a job of its own (ADR-0030), outside that span, **within five minutes**: the same test takes each check at once, as a free worker does, and measures from the request's `finished_at` to the `publication_check` row's `checked_at`, by the database's clock, bound to five minutes where the budget binds - 23.6 seconds for veraPDF's first check, its JVM starting, and 6.2 warm, on the reference configuration, measured with the test suite's veraPDF rather than the worker's own. A check whose first attempt fails still joins within five minutes under the worker's defaults, which `config.test.ts` holds: an attempt ends within its lease, 120 seconds, whether it throws - veraPDF's start and check a third of the lease each - or its worker dies and the lease runs out; the queue retries after 2 seconds and an idle worker asks within a poll, 5 seconds; so a second attempt ends by 120 + 2 + 5 + 120 = 247 seconds. The bound is not held past that - see beside the table

The layout's `contents.depth` reaches Typst's `outline`, which selects the headings the template sets with `number`'s numbers, so the depth is the layout's and only the page is the engine's (decision C of the second slice); `contents(conditioned, numbering, depth)` is what a worker test measures the compiled entries against
The layout's `lists` names sequences; each is one `listOf` call, set like the contents
`contents` and `listOf` take the numbering table made after `conditions`, and the checks and projection read only the conditioned document
A publication has no expiry and no delete route; it is `#/publications/{id}` in the renderer and `GET /v1/publications/{id}` in the API; reading it is `read` decided on the publication artifact
`GET /v1/documents/{id}/publications` lists the document's publications the caller may read, each with its publisher and time, and the document page shows them

The creation time, the request's, is the one value that varies: Typst sets it in the PDF's document information and metadata, with the identifier it makes from it, and the template prints it nowhere; Word's package carries no date
`publication`, `publication_input` and `publication_output` take inserts only; publishing again inserts another publication

Resolve and compose never stop at a failure: each records it and carries on over what remains, and the request answers the whole list. Typst runs only on a document with none, and is handed nothing it would refuse

The publication row, its artifact row and its outputs are inserted in one transaction after every output is stored; a failed request has none. An object stored before a failure is referenced by nothing, and no link can be signed for it
The publication records the engine and its version, the template's name and version, and the pipeline's version

Decision A: every T1 publication is a draft; the template sets **Not approved** on every page as a pagination artifact and the full sentence once as tagged text, and the record says `approval: 'none'`
Every failure names its stage - `resolve`, `compose`, `engine` or `store` - its code, and the node, block, reference or definition it concerns ([Failure](#failure-retry-and-what-an-author-sees))

The regression corpus - the spike's nine cases, grown by a case for every defect, named by its issue - is compiled on every change to the template, the engine or `assemble`, and each case holds its expected outcome, and where it is a question of structure its veraPDF verdict ([Verification](#verification))
A layout's `matter` declares a cover, a contents and whether appendices start on a new page ([The layout](#the-layout))

Decision C: the request resolves every occurrence restricted to what the publisher may read, in the query; one they may not read is `occurrence_unreadable`, naming its node and nothing else, and compose never reads it
A request names one source and a non-empty set of formats; the publication records the set, and publishing the same source to another format is another request and another publication

A request whose formats exclude `pdf` is refused `page_reference_without_pdf` where the resolved document holds a `page` cross-reference those formats would print as a page: any, where Word is asked for; for HTML alone, one declaring no form without pages (Ken, HT-G), since HTML prints the form one declares and so cites no page. Otherwise the absence of a PDF is the record that no output is page-cited

Where no node survives conditions, the document publishes the front and back matter its layout declares that has something to show - a cover, or a contents with entries - and otherwise fails `nothing_to_publish`

Every lossy export says what it could not carry as it is produced: PDF, Word and HTML in the publication's report (`OUTPUT_REPORT_KINDS`), the environment export in its manifest, XLIFF by keeping all as placeholders, and the bibliography's BibTeX and RIS in the export's answer (citations.md, "The export")
The scheme is declared by the layout (here) and applied by `number` (structure.md); the numbering route and the panel number with the document's layout's scheme
The caption's text is the component's; its label is the layout scheme's rule, and its number is `number`'s

`assemble` prints `number`, `title` and `numberAndTitle` from resolution (structure.md's `referenceResolver`); the template prints `page`, from `counter(page).at` at the target's label, in its matter's own numbering; `relative` is the layout's `above` or `below` by document order, which layout schema 3 adds (structure.md, XR-C). Each is read back from the PDF

`assemble` resolves every reference in the document it publishes, and each whose target the document does not hold - or a `component` target whose component it places never or twice - fails `cross_reference_unresolved` at `compose`, naming the occurrence, the reference as its block and its stored target in `detail`, never the author's text; any fails the publish
A format that is not paged (`PAGED`, its kind: HTML) has no page breaks in its projection, and nothing reports their absence ([HTML](#html))
`number` is pure over the outline, the layout's scheme and the profile; the publication pins the first two and records the numbering table it published, in full
In a format that is not paged, a `page` reference renders its `withoutPages` form, and one with none fails `page_reference_without_pages`, naming it, where that format is asked for ([HTML](#html))
A footnote anchored to a cell whose key or position the table does not hold fails `footnote_anchor_unresolved`, naming the footnote and its component
One converter turns stored MathML into the maths tree both writers read; an element it does not know fails `equation_unrenderable`, naming the block, before either writer runs

A citation resolves against a bibliography entry, and in T1 there are none (LIB is T6): the built publish fails every citation as `inline_not_publishable`, detail `citation`, naming its block and its component. Resolution, with LIB, fails one whose entry cannot be resolved as `citation_unresolved`, naming the citation, its entry, its block and its component
As PUB-034: each run's language reaches the published document, and each writer emits it

A table with no caption is refused at publish, naming it (`table_without_caption`), numbered or not; a captioned one takes the outline's number, STR-071's, unless its author marked it unnumbered, when it is set under its caption alone and left out of the list of tables - in the PDF by template 14, which does not outline it, and in Word by writing no `SEQ` field for it ([Tables](#tables))
A table's caption is set by the `figure` it stands in, which Typst tags as a `Caption` inside the `Table`, first, above it or below - measured; Word names the table by its caption in `w:tblCaption`

Header rows are one `table.header(repeat: true)`: they repeat on every page the table reaches and stay one header row in the structure tree - measured; Word's `w:tblHeader` both repeats and marks them

`assemble` resolves a figure's alternative text before the engine runs: `inherited` reads the asset version's default, and a figure whose asset version has none, and which neither carries its own nor is decorative, fails `alternative_missing`, naming it - measured, the engine would refuse the document without saying which figure

Header rows are `TH`s of a column in the PDF and `w:tblHeader` rows in Word; a header column's cells are `pdf.header-cell(scope: "row")` `TH`s in the PDF - measured - and in Word, which has no header column, the publication's report names each table whose header column it could not mark (word-output.md)

A table is one `Table` in the structure tree, a `TR` for each row in order and `TH`s for its headers, and set with `breakable: true` it breaks across pages as that one `Table` - measured under [Tables](#tables)
The stream is opened by an authenticated request; a permission change ends it, and the reconnect is authorised afresh
Stated plainly: individual events are not guaranteed and are not replayed; the picture is, because every connect begins with a snapshot
The snapshot on connect, events held until it is sent, and events applied as state
Measured by the conformance suite with the spike's harness: every delivery, to every entitled viewer, at stepped rates
