Presence names each person in the document and the component they are in

Presence carries the mode - read, review or author - from the document view (CNT-104); the page beats `read` or `author`, as review mode (CNT-155) is not built, and the mode is said, not checked against permission
A person in a component the viewer may not read is reported only as present in the document, component and mode removed
Presence lasts while its window beats; a closed stream removes its viewer at once, and a silent one is stale then absent (PL-C)
Each presence event carries when it was beaten; a viewer shows it live under 30 seconds, stale to 60, then absent
The events are declared in zod and published as AsyncAPI 3.0 beside `openapi.json`, drift-checked, every event a test receives parsed against it (PL-E)
Lock events and the snapshot carry the holder and the expected release, wherever the component is shown
Presence, locks and notifications are each a message of the AsyncAPI document, apart from OpenAPI: `inbox` says a notification waits, on every stream its recipient holds
The Cite dialog's **Search** tab queries a configured source and inserts a citation from a result, matched or made as an entry
Sources are a declared, versioned list in domain; a further one is an extension of kind `reference`
Check now and the nightly sweep re-check an entry: whether it resolves, which fields differ, and a retraction, supersession or correction; when it ran
A retraction or correction is flagged on each citation and its document's owner told; a gate condition can refuse the move
The assistant's `search_references` and `cite_reference` tools, as the calling person; the entry made, and the citation inserted, when a person accepts

A relationship names its type, a definition of kind `relationshipType`, and is refused `type.missing` where none is declared ([the R8 plan](../plans/2026-10-16-r8-relationships-and-the-graph.md), R8-A)
The type declares its `inverseName`, read whenever a relationship is read from its far end
A type is a definition, made and changed through `/v1/definitions` by whoever manages the environment's definitions, as fields are
A definition is never deleted, so a type in use cannot be; a change that would break its relationships is refused (REL-054)
Each end's kind is held to the kinds the type permits there, in the transaction that writes the relationship (`endsRefused`)
Its values are checked against the fields its type's schemas assign, before it is written
Cardinality is counted under an advisory lock on the type and each limited end, so two at once cannot both find room
Each end names the version it pins, or none and floats at latest
Making, changing and removing a relationship are audited `relationship.made`, `.changed` and `.removed`, on its from end, naming its type and itself (R8-E)
A relationship's values are changed whole, and either end re-targeted or re-pinned
A change is checked exactly as making it is: kinds, self-reference, cardinality, cycles and values
Making, changing or removing one needs read on both ends and the permission its type declares at each; reading it, read on both
A type marked `deprecated`, naming a replacement or none, is refused for new relationships and stays valid on those that hold it
A type is renamed by its next version, its identifier unchanged, so its relationships are untouched
A type declares at each end whether an artifact may hold one relationship of it there, or many
Each end pins or floats on its own
A relationship from an artifact to itself is refused unless its type declares `selfReference`
Where a type is `acyclic`, a relationship whose to end already reaches its from end along the type is refused, under a lock on the type

The type declares its name, its stable identifier (the definition's), its endpoint kinds, direction, inverse name, cardinality, self-reference, acyclicity, the permission at each end, whether it is informational, and its schemas
As REL-012: the lock makes the count and the insert one act
A type assigns metadata schemas, as a component type does, whose fields its relationships carry
A type's next version is refused where it would leave relationships invalid, saying how many
Foreign keys to `artifact` restrict deletion; removing an artifact's relationships is an explicit, audited act that deletion awaits
The neighbours operation, by type and direction, at most 1,000
Every operation requires a depth, and the service refuses anything above ten
De-duplicating recursion never revisits an artifact at a depth it has already reached, so a cycle ends the walk rather than repeating
The permission test is inside the recursive step, so an unreadable artifact is never returned and never expanded
Edges into the walk from unreadable artifacts are counted, and every result carries whether any were
Impact walks references and relationships together, from the artifact outwards along edges into it
Each artifact in an impact result is marked hard if a chain of references alone reaches it, and informational otherwise

Hard impact is the cheap walk - 76ms at worst in the spike - so it runs before a change is made: Save version, Done editing and approving a component each say first the documents a version reaches and what reaches it through relationships, three hops out (the R19 plan, R19-C)
The shortest-path operation: a bidirectional search to a declared depth, optionally along named types
The Relationships dialog draws an artifact's relationships centred on it, and Expand reads the next ring
The dialog filters by type and direction, the service answering each filter
Past twenty neighbours of one kind from one artifact, the graph draws a count, opened as a list
Every view names the `GET` query that answers it, filters and all
Neighbours and the dialog filter by one field's value, as well as by type and direction
Results stop at the nearest 1,000, and the result says whether there are more
The conformance suite generates a tenant like the spike's and measures every operation for three kinds of user
The impact report runs in the background with no result cap, bounded by depth and filtered by permission
The report is a job (service-foundations.md, "Jobs"): its identity at once, pollable with its depth reached, cancellable at its next depth, failing in an error's shape
A reference names a component the author may read, from any space (`mayReference`); `GET /v1/components/{id}/uses` lists every document placing it
Each reference is its own outline node, so one component placed twice is two occurrences, each listed apart
A reference to a component deleted, or none at all, fails the publish `occurrence_gone`, naming its node
One there that the publisher may not read fails `occurrence_unreadable`, naming its node alone; only the gone are selected, so nothing of it is read
Save version reads the uses first, and asks before a version reaching any `latest` or `approved` reference, listing each document it reaches; working changes reach none
Each document in the uses carries whether its workflow state is approved, and the warning lists approved documents apart from drafts
Each reference in where-used says whether it carries local overrides

"Where is this used" is the reference index read backwards, one hop, for components (`/v1/components/{id}/uses`), query definitions, assets and templates (`/impact?depth=1`, and each kind's own uses route); a style, named by its kind and key, reads the latest component versions naming it (`GET /v1/styles/uses`; the R20 plan, R20-A) - a scan of the tenant's components at each ask, one style at a time, which a block-style index would replace at scale
Each reference is listed with its mode: `latest` takes every new version, `approved` each approved revision, `pinned` none
Where-used applies the same permission test as traversal
As REU-006, for any referenced artifact
"What does this use" is the reference index read forwards, one hop
Structural queries use the same permission test as traversal, which is the one search applies (ADR-0016)
The permission set is computed for each search and applied as a predicate inside the query, never to a result list afterwards
Counts and facets are aggregates over the same predicate as the results, in the same query
The projection lives in the tenant's schema, and the search role can reach no other (ADR-0008)
Permissions are read at each search, so a change applies to the next one. The stated delay is none
Every filtering path has a test that searches as a user who may read nothing matching, and asserts empty results and zero counts
Meaning is searched in the same query as words, restricted by the same predicate
Every result carries a label: matched words, meaning, or both
The projection is rebuilt from current versions and the embedding store; nothing in it exists anywhere else
Without the embedding model, search returns the words half and says meaning is unavailable; without the database, it says so
Ranking may use tenant-wide statistics; the predicate still applies before results, counts and facets are computed

The budget is measured against a generated tenant of a million components, for three kinds of user, by the load suite's search profile (`packages/db/src/load/search.load.ts`), run by hand: the words through their indexes, the definitions through theirs, ranking and facets bounded and the road chosen (SV3)

Counting stops at the cap, over the visible rows, and the interface returns the count as a lower bound; past the bound, facets count the 1,000 most recently changed visible matches, each shown as a lower bound ([Counts and facets](#counts-and-facets))
The vector strategy is chosen by the size of the visible set, and a test asserts a full page for a user who can see very little

Every kind the product holds is a `search_entry` - a component, a document, each of its sections, a publication, a template, an asset, a field, a metadata schema and a component type - written with the version that makes it what it is ([Searching words, in T1](#searching-words-in-t1))
Each entry's text is its content's every block - a caption and a figure's alternative text among them - its title, and its values rendered as words, each a `search_text` row of its own

A query is Postgres's web search syntax - a phrase in quotes, `-word` excluding, `or` - and a term written `name:word` or `name:"a phrase"` is looked for only in the place `name` names: `title`, or a metadata field by its name
Query and text are both NFC-normalised, as ingest normalises content (CNT-056), and both folded by the same text search configuration, so two strings a reader cannot tell apart match
Every result carries a passage from the place it matched, the matched words marked, cut to about thirty words
Every result names the place it matched - a block of a component, a section of a document, a field's value - and links to it there

A query with nothing to search for, one that excludes and asks for nothing, a scope naming no field, and a phrase left open are each answered by a named outcome with a sentence, never an error page, never the whole corpus and never an empty page

The facet dimensions are declared: kind, space, component type, owner, when it last changed in five named ranges, and each metadata field whose data type facets - a boolean, a person, a date by month, a text of one value. Each dimension's counts are computed with every other filter in force and its own left out

A result links by identity - the artifact's id and the place's own id, never a position. Where the place is no longer in the version the reader opens, the page says so by name and shows the version it opened, which is the newest
Results are narrowed by kind, space, a metadata value, owner - who made the artifact - and a date range, each a filter over the same predicate
Component type is a filter and a facet over components; a field facets across every entry whose values hold it - a component's, a document's, a section's - however it came to hold it

The latest version by default; on request every version, from one `search_history` row a place, or what one baseline pins: earlier versions' rows kept in `search_earlier`, read only when asked, the latest's query unchanged ([Earlier versions and baselines](#earlier-versions-and-baselines))
A result from an earlier version names it and links to that version's read-only page at its place; one found in a baseline, to the baseline's page at its node

A thread is one `search_entry` on the artifact it is anchored to, so the one predicate filters it; each message a `search_text` place, appended to the entry as it is written and an edit rebuilt from the entry's own places, never by re-reading the thread ([Threads](#threads))
`internal=true` or `false` keeps threads alone, internal or not; for a searcher from outside the organisation an internal thread is no row at all, in results, facets and counts (the R13 plan, R13-D)

An entry's rows are written in the transaction that writes its version, so new and changed words are findable the moment the version is: the interval is none, measured by a test that searches in the next transaction

A section result carries its document, by id and title, and each component placed beneath it that the reader may read, once in outline order, read from the document version it matched in and titled from the entries now; the page links each and offers **Place in a document**, REU-054's act with the destination chosen (the R14 plan, R14-C)

An entry's `field_values` hold every `axis:value` its content is conditioned on under `~conditions` - a component's blocks' and marks', a document's every node's, a section's own and those beneath it - read with `conditionsIn`, nothing resolved under a profile; `condition=<axis>:<value>` filters, several of one axis either and several axes all, served by 0110's index, and each axis facets, its own filter left out (the R14 plan, R14-D)

A component's or a document's entry holds, under `~relations`, each field value of every relationship its artifact is an end of, with the type and the other end; `related=<type>:<field>:<value>` filters and each type's field facets as a field's values do, a value said only of a relationship whose type, field and other end the reader may read. Making, changing or removing a relationship writes both ends' entries again, and an end it moved from (R14-E)

A latest version is recorded in `embedding_lag` once no block of it lacks a passage for the serving model, at indexing where every block is reused, else after its embedding job, from its cut; nothing while none serves or one is pending. `GET /v1/search/meaning/freshness` answers, and Models shows, the last seven days' p95 and most, nearest-rank; a worker test measures 20 versions against 60 s and 300 s (the FR plan, FR-E)
Authority comes from the session found; the hostname only chooses where to look, and a session exists only in the tenant that issued it
A shared harness gives every route a test that signs in to one tenant and calls with another's hostname and ids, and must be refused
The organisation's provider is an OpenID Connect authorisation code flow with PKCE, redirecting to each environment's own hostname

A service identity is a principal of kind `service` with no issuer, subject or address, made by an administrator; no sign-in, invitation claim or update makes one from a person, or a person from one (G8)

An API token is a row with explicit scopes, chosen from the closed permission set, and an expiry that cannot be left unset; the scopes mask its creator's grants at every decision, so it can do less than its creator and never more (TK-A)
A token or session is checked against its row on every request, so deleting the row revokes it at once
Signing out deletes the session row, which ends it in every browser and device presenting that cookie

A person sees their own sessions - route, begun, last used, this one - and ends any or all but this one; ending deletes the row, records it and stops what it was doing ([Sessions and tokens](#sessions-and-tokens))
The Google route needs no customer configuration: one product-registered client, returning through `signin.<domain>` to the environment
There is no credential table: principals are identified by their provider's issuer and subject, and no password field exists anywhere
Each tenant records the routes it permits; sign-in offers only those, and closing one ends the sessions it issued
Sign-in requests `openid`, `email` and `profile` and nothing else, and a test pins the scope list
A tenant accepting Google accounts admits only the addresses it invited and the Workspace domains it names; an invitation binds once, by verified email

Every search index, cache, secret and publication store the service and the worker keep is the tenant's own, each shown by a test ([Tenant scope of every store](#tenant-scope-of-every-store)): the search projection, publications with their outputs and checks, and each environment's secrets - its object store credential and sign-in client secret sealed to it, its source credentials sealed by the connector, its sessions' and tokens' hashes - in its schema, which no other tenant's role can read or delete; objects under a credential the store confines to the tenant's prefix; the shared job queue, which a tenant's role may add to only in its own name and never read; and every in-process cache keyed by the tenant, its hostname or its principal, or holding nothing of any tenant's. The platform directory and the logs are outside it
An organisation groups a customer's tenants - production, a sandbox, a validation copy - and holds no content
A hostname table maps any hostname to a tenant: two-level names by default, and a customer's own domain later through the same table
The renderer calls the service only through the client generated from the committed OpenAPI document
Routes are zod schemas; the OpenAPI document is generated from them at build, committed, and the client types generated from it

The renderer reads and changes stored state only through the generated client, which calls only the routes the contract declares; what it converts in the browser - LaTeX to MathML, the spoken alternative, a paste - it stores through those routes like anything else

CI regenerates the document and fails on any difference; Fastify validates every response against its schema, and a status a route does not list against the one error shape the document declares as its `default`, so nothing undeclared is sent; a test holds the routes served to the contract's, both ways

The service publishes the committed OpenAPI document by API major version and a self-hosted reference generated from it; every operation has a description, one navigation tag, its required permission and examples, and the tags belong to a documented group. The reference executes only token-enabled operations, with an explicitly entered personal token kept in memory, never with the browser's session or through another origin
Every error is one JSON shape with a stable `code`, a message, and the request's trace id
The error shape names what failed and, where a rule refused it, the rule's identifier

Every mutation of a versioned resource names the version it was read at - the outline act and the publication request the document's, a save, a cut and a release the component's - and a mismatch is refused `409 version_precondition`, naming the version the resource is at now: the document with its outline for the outline act, the version's heading alone for a publication request, whose outline may name what the caller may not read (IAM-073), and the version's heading for a component
Listings take and return an opaque cursor over a stable order; offsets are never accepted
A mutating request with an `Idempotency-Key` records its response per tenant, and a repeat returns the recorded response
Work that can outlive a request is submitted where its subject is and answered at once with an `api_job`, accepted; the platform queue carries it by id (Jobs, below)
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}`: its state of five, when it started, and its progress, `done` of `of` in a unit, written by the worker in its own transaction at each step
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel`: an accepted job is cancelled at once, having done nothing; a running one stops at its next step, its outcome saying how far it got; a finished one is refused
A failed job keeps `failure`, an error's members but its trace, and stays readable after, as every finished job does
A submit route takes an `Idempotency-Key` as every permission-checked mutating route does (API-008): a retry answers the job the first made

The whole tenant is exported as a job, `POST /v1/exports`, never assembled by paging: one ZIP archive of JSON Lines parts, the bytes they name by hash and a manifest, kept seven days ([The tenant export](#the-tenant-export))

Every listing pages by keyset over its sort key and then the artifact's id, a total order, and is read as of its first page's snapshot - each version and publication knowing the transaction that wrote it - so a walk is over one set no later write moves, and never repeats or skips ([Listings and idempotency, in T1](#listings-and-idempotency-in-t1))

Components, documents, publications and templates each have a listing, a view of it in the application, and server-side sorting and filtering, each filter counted as a facet ([Listings and idempotency, in T1](#listings-and-idempotency-in-t1))
Every path begins with its major version, `/v1`; a breaking change is a new version

Response schemas are open - generated clients ignore fields they do not know - and adding a field is never a new version; the document's description tells every caller to ignore a field it does not know, and that no field is removed within the version

Every response carries `X-Request-Id`: the caller's own where it sent a plain token of at most 128 characters, a fresh one otherwise, set on every response by one hook and on the event stream's own head. It is the request's trace id, so every log line and every error body carries the same value
An `iteration` row carries editor, timestamp, content and metadata values, and is never updated after insert
Iterations are readable only by the editor holding the component's lock, and of those only the holder's own: a later holder never reads an earlier one's (component-editor.md, RC-A)

Promotion deletes nothing. An iteration is kept until the next version after the one it was opened from is cut, and for the tenant's window after that cut: the sweep removes it only once that version's cut time and the window have passed, and nothing is decided at insert, when the cut has not happened (the T1 audit's defect; RC-B)

The window is a tenant setting, `iteration_retention_days`, 30 by default, read when the sweep and the Recovery listing run: a longer window keeps what has not been swept longer, and nothing swept comes back (RC-C)
Nothing outside the editor's own recovery view joins to `iteration`. No foreign key points at it, which is what keeps it out of comparison and audit
A version row is inserted by promotion from an iteration, never by the autosave path
Author, timestamp and optional note are columns on the version row
`artifact_version` takes inserts only. No update or delete grant exists on it for the application role
`revision_no` and `version_no` are columns on the version row; the pair renders as `revision.version`
`schema_version` is a column on the version row, written at insert from the schema the content was authored against
One versioning mechanism parameterised by `artifact_kind`, so documents - one kind, whose content is the outline - assets, themes, layouts and templates share it
A revision is a designation row referring to an existing version, adding no content of its own
Only the lifecycle service may insert a designation, and it does so as part of passing a gate
Designator, timestamp and gate are columns on the designation row

`revision_no` counts from 1 within an artifact; a version never designated carries revision 0; a divergent line's versions are stored below the main line's and present as the revision they count from ([Lines](#lines))
The designation row is insert-only on the same terms as the version row
A `baseline` row names a document artifact and a moment, and is insert-only
`baseline_pin` holds one foreign key per pinned artifact version, covering every kind VER-011 versions

A component's divergent line, `artifact_line`, names the designated revision it diverged from and when; its versions are its own head, numbered below the main line's, its workflow and scope its own; `GET /v1/components/{id}/lines` lists them to any reader ([Lines](#lines))

A line is brought back only after `GET .../lines/{line}/comparison`, naming both heads and each block that differs, and only from those heads: the author takes the line's side of each block carried; the main line gets a new version, the line closes, and `line_return` records each block carried and left behind, audited `line.returned` - never an overwrite ([Lines](#lines))

A component with an open line says so wherever it appears: its page's **Line** names every line and which is read; its list row and its search result say **Diverged** with the lines' names; each reference in a document says the line the version shown is on, or **Main line; also** the others ([Lines](#lines))
`baseline_value` holds each bound value and its provenance, pinned at the same instant as the versions

The profile in force is the one the pinned document version declares, so it is in the baseline's digest already; the baseline's view says it, and its publication records it and is made under it (the R11 plan, R11-F)
Baseline creation is an explicit call, made by a person; a gate's call (VER-059) is T9's
Everything a baseline pins is reachable by foreign key, and nothing reachable that way is collectable

`baseline_pin` restricts deletion of the version it references. The database refuses, rather than application code remembering to check; a tombstone removes no row, so its refusal is checked in code ([lifecycle.md](lifecycle.md))
Restore reads an earlier version and inserts a new one with matching content. The earlier row is untouched
The new version records the version it was restored from, so the chain reads as a decision
Preview resolves the restore without inserting, using the same code path as the write
Versions, revisions and baselines have no expiry of their own; retention is a policy decision applied above this layer
Derived data records the model and model version that produced it
Re-deriving inserts new derived rows and alters no version

A component artifact carries its identifier; each version row carries its component type's version and `schema_version`, and content whose root holds the title and base language (CNT-146). There is no general attribute column, so adding a structural attribute is a migration
Metadata values are a column on the version row, which takes inserts only, so a value changes only by a new version; `baseline_pin` pins the version, and the values with it
Values are held in their own column beside `content`, and the content document's closed root (CNT-146) refuses a member that is not its own
Every version row records a version digest - SHA-256 over the canonical serialisation of the version's substance - which anybody holding the row can recompute (ADR-0024)
A document artifact's content is one `outline` document; its root holds one ordered array of nodes and there is nowhere to put a second

Placing another document's section reports first how many occurrences it makes, each component it places with its blocks and characters now, and how many the author may not read (`previewPlacement`; the R2 plan, R2-F)

A placement adds a new section of the author's, titled by them, holding one new reference per occurrence in the found section's subtree in the mode chosen; nothing is shared and no value copied; refused where the source moved since the report or a component is not the author's to reference

A reference's `overrides` replace a paragraph's text of its component in this document alone, at most twenty: text runs and their marks, so no number, binding, footnote or cross-reference changes ([the R4 plan](../plans/2026-10-15-r4-local-overrides.md), R4-A)
Overrides are a member of the reference node, set by the outline's `set` whole; the component is never written
An override applies only where its paragraph is canonically as it stood at `against`; otherwise it is stale: the publish fails `override_stale`, naming node and block, and the texts say so beside it

The outline's root holds the document's `profile`: its values on each condition axis, and `excludeUnset` where it accepts exclusion by an unset axis; written whole by `PUT /v1/documents/{id}/profile`, refused where it names an axis or value nothing declares, and carried by every other write (the R6 plan, R6-B)
`node` is a closed discriminated union of `section` and `reference`. A third arm is a schema version with a migration
`id` is required on every node, allocated from 128 random bits at insertion, spelled by the domain, and never reused - nothing reissues, because nothing recycles
A section is a node inside one outline document. It has no artifact row, so there is no identity to share it by and no route that could return one
The outline panel reorders by pointer and by an enumerated keymap, and the same five operations are the routes below. All three go through one set of operations
Nesting is the tree's own, bounded by the parse at 64 levels - far above nine - so no stored outline is too deep to read; the numbering scheme's counters are a stack rather than nine named members
A move names a node, a new parent and a position among its siblings; the subtree travels because it _is_ the subtree, and the whole move is one version and one undo entry
Two nodes may name one component. Each is a node with its own `id`, and every occurrence-bearing thing below - numbering, captions, references - is keyed by the node, not the component
The outline is the document version's content, so every change to it is a new version of the document; `baseline_pin` pins a document version like any other (VER-018)
`sequences` is an open map from a name to its rule, with `section`, `figure`, `table` and `equation` always present. A further sequence is a member, not a code change
A sequence's rule carries `restartAt`, an outline depth. The engine's counter stack drops every counter below that depth on entering a node at it
A top-level node carries `matter`, inherited by its subtree; a sequence declares a rule per matter, so an appendix numbers in its own scheme with its own `restartAt`

The outline parse refuses a `front` node below the top level, or after any top-level node that is not front matter, naming the node; every operation's result goes back through that parse, and an operation that would break the order is refused in words of its own
A node carries `numbered`, and an unnumbered node is walked for its children and never increments a counter
`number(conditioned, scheme)` is pure: no clock, no identifiers minted, no iteration order that depends on anything but the tree
No number is representable. The content model has no member for one, the outline holds switches rather than values, and the numbering table is returned rather than written
The engine walks occurrences, not components. A component referenced twice is two walks over one content document, and its captions take two numbers

Every entry in the numbering table names the node that produced it, the block where it is a caption or a footnote, the sequence and the matter, the section counter stack at that point, its own counter's value and the node that last restarted it; the rule applied is named by the table's scheme with the entry's sequence and matter
Resolution reads the numbering table, which is built for one document. The component is never consulted: it holds a target, and targets carry no answer

Nothing caches a number. The numbering table is computed from the outline, each occurrence's resolved component version and the scheme whenever it is asked for, and every answer names each occurrence's version. A cache, when one is needed, is keyed by the document version, every occurrence's resolved component version, the scheme and the profile - the document's digest alone misses a `latest` component's new head. That a stale number cannot be rendered is answered in [Cross-references](#cross-references): a cross-reference has no member for a number, so there is none to go stale
A `block` target reaches a block or footnote of the reference's own component; a `component` target reaches a block or footnote of another component of the same document
A `block` target carries no occurrence, and resolution binds it to the occurrence being read, so one stored reference resolves once per occurrence

Resolution binds a `block` target to the occurrence being read and a `component` target to that component's one occurrence, and returns a failure naming the reference and its target where there are none or several - never the first
The panel calls the same `number` the publisher calls, with the same scheme, so the two cannot disagree - not by agreement, but by being one function
Reordering in the panel is the move operation, from the panel's own drag and from its keymap

The contents mark what matters to an author on each node's row, said to a screen reader as its description: who else holds its component, from the document's stream; the broken references its text draws; the values its bindings failed to hold (the PL plan, PL-J)

The document route, the contributions route, the numbering route and an outline act are each measured in the service suite over a document of 500 nodes and 400 occurrences, against p95 250 ms and a maximum of 500 ms, after five warm-up calls that are not measured samples, with the configuration recorded beside the result. A run on a named machine is held to both; a run on a shared CI runner, whose speed varies by more than the budget itself, records both and is held to neither (issues #179 and #188), so a green CI run does not show the budget met

Opened from within the application - from the documents list, the interface already running - and every act the outline offers are measured in the browser suite (`tests/browser/src/budgets.test.ts`) over STR-063's document, the interface's share against p90 250 ms and a maximum of 500 ms, on the reference machine, whose configuration each run records beside its samples
`contents(conditioned, numbering, depth)` lists every node to the depth, numbered or not, a reference's title left to its caller
`listOf(conditioned, numbering, sequence)` lists one sequence's entries with their captions
A node's URL is the document's path and the node's identifier, both identifiers
The URL holds no depth, no number and no position, so there is nothing in it for a reorder to invalidate
A node carries `pageBreak`: none, a new page, or a new recto page
`pageBreak` is a member of the node. The content model has no member for one, so the declaration cannot travel with the component
The four stages are one function each, and each takes the previous stage's return type. Calling them out of order does not typecheck

An identifier is 128 random bits in the spelling `blockIdentifierFrom` already fixes, validated unique within its outline at every write. Across documents the argument is the one the product already makes for a UUID
Before a version is recorded, a reachability walk from the document over the reference index refuses a cycle with `outline_cycle`, naming the path
A reference node carries `mode`: `pinned` with a version, `latest`, or `approved`. The three are closed, and absent is not a fourth

Every operation carries the version it was read at and is answered `version_precondition` with the current outline when it is not the latest; `component_lock` refuses a document by a check constraint, so no document lock can be introduced by accident

The root is the document artifact, which carries the identity a top-level deep link addresses, and `nodes` has no minimum - unlike content's, which CNT-124 gives one. The deep link itself (STR-044) is not built, so the cited test shows the empty outline and the root's identity and no link: that clause is answered by the design and demonstrated by nothing yet

A document is an artifact of its own kind: its identity is the `artifact` row, `artifact_space_by_kind` puts it in exactly one space, its title lives inside its versioned content as a component's does, and it versions through the one mechanism
`footnote` is a sequence in the scheme like any other, counted over the resolved document rather than within a component
The model's `numbered` decides whether a block equation takes from the equation sequence; an unnumbered one is walked and never increments it

The engine takes each occurrence's figures, tables and block equations in document order and increments the sequence for the kind: a figure or a table takes a number unless the model marks it `numbered: false`, and a block equation unless the model marks it unnumbered (CNT-047); an unnumbered one is walked, contributes `numbered: false`, is no numbering entry, moves no counter and so is in no generated list; a reference to an unnumbered figure or table binds to its caption with no label, so a title form prints the caption and a number form fails by name; and a caption met in front or appendix matter before that matter's first numbered section - where its rule wants a chapter prefix and there is none - takes none and uses up none

A reference's `mode` - the latest version, or one pinned - is a switch an outline `set` changes, and every act on an outline is recorded as a new version of the document in the version chain, naming its author and when it was made, with the whole outline as it then stood: so which version a document referenced before a change and after it are both read back from the chain. The audited act is CNT-182's, below

Changing which version a reference takes is audited `reference.repointed` `{ node, component, from, to }` (modes; `packages/db/src/documents.ts`, `recordRepoints`), in the transaction of the version recording it, so who and when are the event's own: the outline's `set` changing a reference's mode, and a document's restore for each reference it re-points. Insert, remove and move are not re-points, and a `latest` reference meeting a newer version is no act (the RS plan, RS-G)
The same event says from which to which: a pinned side its version, and an `approved` side the version its latest revision then is (the WF4 plan, WF4-D)

Numbering never reads a component the reader may not read (`numberingInputs`), so its occurrence is unknown and `number` answers `null` for each number it could have moved: every counter in its matter, until that counter next restarts, whatever it holds ([Who is shown what](#who-is-shown-what)). A section number depends on the outline alone

A reference's target is a closed union - `node` for an outline node, `block` and `component` for a caption-bearing block or a footnote - each naming its target by identifier, never by number or position; a component may hold a `node` target (XR-B), so body text can point at a section

`incomingReferences` binds every reference in the document's section titles and readable texts as `referenceResolver` does, and answers for a node each reference to it or to anything in it from outside it, computed in the page from the texts it already reads, no index and no request of its own. The Part panel lists each referring place as a link, and removing a referenced node names them before it is confirmed, never refused. A text the reader may not read is never read, and a withheld occurrence names no component a reference could bind to (SCH-032)

The contents panel is the outline, rendered: it renders the outline every operation returns rather than a copy of one, so it updates with every act the author makes, and clicking a node takes the reader to it ([Navigation](#navigation))

Another person's change reaches the contents as it happens: the document's stream says its outline changed, and the panel reads it again once no act of the reader's own is in flight, which answers with the outline as it then stands (the PL plan, PL-J)

A node's details offer **Used in** for each component it places, itself where a reference or every one beneath it where a section, that the reader may read, each opening the component's where-used (REU-006), which names every document placing it. Nothing in another document refers to a node but through its component: a cross-reference stays within its document (the R14 plan, R14-B)
Every container reaches tenant data only through that tenant's database role, scoped object-storage credentials and tenant channel - see below

The desktop app loads `ALLOY_SERVICE_URL`, else the address kept from its Connect to screen, else that screen; the tray and an address not answering ask again ([ADR-0072](../decisions/0072-the-desktop-app-asks-which-environment.md))
A close publishes a Windows installer, its blockmap and `latest.yml` as GitHub release `vX.Y.Z`, built after CI passes on that commit ([ci-and-releases.md](../ci-and-releases.md#releases))

On Windows, packaged, the shell checks GitHub's releases after start and from the tray, offers a newer one by its version, downloads it only when agreed and installs it on Restart now or the next quit; decided in `shell.ts` (`updateStep`) ([DR plan](../plans/2026-10-31-dr-desktop-releases.md), DR-H, DR-I)
`columns` lists the result columns shown, in order ([The presentation](#the-presentation))
Each column carries its `header`, required, defaulting in the editor to the column's name
A column's `unit` prints in its header, bracketed as the table style says, or after each value where the column asks
A column the dataset version does not have is `column_missing`, in the page and at the stage, never an empty column
Every declaration lives in the block and names a column by the result's column name, never a position; T3's declarations follow the same rule
A column named twice is refused unless every header naming it differs, `column_repeated`
With no `sort`, rows print in the dataset version's stored order: the definition's declared order, or for a multiset the canonical order data.md stores
`sort` is stable over the stored order, so ties keep it and never swap between runs ([Order](#order))
No rows prints the headers and the declared empty statement spanning the table
A column's format is the table style's format for its type, overridden by the column's ([Formatting](#formatting))
Number, currency, percentage, date, time, duration and unit
`places` per column, applied to every value in it
`rounding` is declared, half away from zero or half to even, and stated in provenance
`negative`: a minus sign or parentheses, and optionally the style's negative colour beside either, never alone
`null` prints declared text, which may not be empty or a number; an empty text cell prints empty
Formatting reads the canonical value and changes nothing; provenance records each printed cell's canonical value
The override merges property by property ([Formatting](#formatting))
A unit labels; no format converts a quantity
Separators and date order come from the value catalogue's formats for the document's language (BI-F)
A number column aligns on its decimal separator by layout, not by added characters; alignment by type is the table style's
A column declares `wrap: false` where it must not wrap: its cells are set on one line in the PDF and carry `w:noWrap` in Word
A note anchors to a cell by the definition's key and a column ([Notes](#notes))
A note anchors to a column; the table's `note` is the note on the whole table
Notes in any table, bound or authored, are lettered in the table's own sequence and printed beneath it
`source`, inline content printed beneath the table after a layout word
`wide`: `scale` or `rotate`, the table style's default, applied to every table, bound or authored ([Wide tables](#wide-tables))
A scaled or rotated table is one tagged table and one Word table
A note by key needs a definition declaring a key: `key_required` where it is placed
A block binding produces a table whose presentation is this block's and the table style's, never the binding's
A table's values are formatted by its table style over the value catalogue, the same declaration bindings.md formats an inline value by; neither is stored in the binding
A note whose row the result no longer has is `note_row_missing`, naming the note, the key and the definition, in the page and at the stage

A revision to a cell names its row by key and its column; its row gone is `revision_row_missing`, naming the revision, the key and the definition, in the page and at the stage ([Revised cells](#revised-cells))
An empty result where the definition declares one valid prints headers and the statement; declared invalid, the run already failed (DAT-068)
A note into generated content names its row by key value, never by position
`groups` names a column; each group opens with a heading row ([Groups](#groups))
Up to three groups, outermost first; groups order first, the sort within each

A heading keeps with its group's first row; in the PDF it repeats on each page its group continues on, so a subtotal never begins a page without it, and in Word a subtotal keeps with its group's last row ([Groups](#groups))
The reshaping here is `groups` and `transpose`, nothing else ([Transposition](#transposition))
Each is a member of the block, shown on the Table tab and recorded in provenance
Grouping and transposing move values and add none: a heading prints a value its rows hold, a subtotal is the query's row
The table style's `widths`, `equal` or `content`, computed once and set alike by the editor, the PDF and Word; a no-wrap column as wide as its widest cell ([Widths](#widths))
`template` is an artifact kind whose artifact belongs to exactly one space; its payload carries a `name`, and each change is a version cut by `recordVersion` under the rules every artifact follows
A template definition has exactly one `theme`, one `layout` and one `outline` member, each required, and a `schemas` array of zero or more assignments

The outline is held inside the definition, so it is versioned with the template and changes only with it; the theme, the layout and every schema are named by artifact identifier and resolved where they are used, never copied

Making a document resolves the template's theme, layout and schemas to their latest versions, and each `requires` against its schema's latest version; any that does not resolve refuses the request, `template_unresolved`, naming what did not, and nothing is written
The starting outline is an ordered tree of sections; making a document writes them as its first outline, in that order
A starting section may be `required`; a publication request for a document with no section carrying that section's key is refused, `section_required`, naming each missing section by its title

A definition's `changes` says whether sections may be added, removed and reordered; the outline act reads the document's recorded template version and refuses an insert, a removal or a move of a section that `changes` forbids, naming the rule

Each assignment is `{ schema, level, requires }`: `level` is `document` or `section`, and `requires` names fields the schema groups, which is the component type's MET-009 shape and so can make a field required and do nothing else

Making a document from a template writes its starting outline and seeds the document's values and each starting section's from their effective fields' defaults and fixed values, by the same `carryForward` a component's first version uses
Making a document records, beside the document, the template and the template version it was made from, once and never changed
After it is made, the document's outline is its own: every outline act changes the document and none reaches the template, and a template's later versions change no document already made
The starting outline is copied into the document when it is made, never shared: the document's outline acts change only the document, and the template's later versions change no document (TPL-027)

A publication request resolves the document-level fields its template applies and validates the document's values, then each section's against the section-level fields, and is refused, `metadata_invalid`, listing every failure in MET-022's shape with the section it belongs to
A template's `parameters` declare name, type, whether required, and permitted values or range, by the query definition's own declaration ([Parameters](#parameters))
Making a document refuses a required parameter without a value, `parameter_invalid`, and writes nothing
A document version holds its `parameters`; the Parameters panel and its route show each value and every change with who made it and when
Each parameter declares `changeable`; changing one that is not is `parameter_fixed`
Making a document, its parameters included, is the same route for the form and for any other client, and refuses alike
Every value is checked by the definitions' `checkParameterValues` at creation, change and resolve, and refused naming the parameter, the rule and the value
A parameter seeds its declared document field when the document is made, and supplies a binding's `{ document }` argument at resolve and check, a changed value marking the binding changed
`feeds` declares the field a parameter seeds and whether it supplies arguments; one feeding nothing is `parameter_unused`

A section carries its title, as it does, and field values in its `values`, written by the outline act's `set`, each checked against the section-level fields of the document's template and refused by name where it is not one of them or does not pass

The document's view lists its departures from its recorded template version, to a reader of the template: each section with no `origin` the template names, and each starting section none came from, a required one with the reason it was removed ([Governance](#governance))

The outline's `remove` of a subtree holding a section from a required starting section needs a `reason`, kept as a `section_waiver` row (0100) and audited `section.waived`; a restore removing one is refused ([Governance](#governance))

A document moves to its template's newest version only by `POST /v1/documents/{id}/template-move`, on edit and the template's read, against the document version its author previewed; insert-only `document_template_move` (0101), audited `template.moved`; never forced, refused at the newest already or to any other version ([Governance](#governance))

`GET .../template-move?to=` answers what the move would change, recording nothing, from the resolution the move repeats; the page shows it before **Move**, and **Keep** leaves it ([Governance](#governance))

The move brings the newer version's assignments forward and carries values by `carryForward`; the report names each field assigned, no longer assigned, or made required or not, at document and section level, and each value not carried, as MET-036 does. Fields resolve current (TE-K), so a changed schema or field applies without a move, which is therefore never needed for one ([Governance](#governance))

`POST /v1/spaces/{space}/cohorts` makes a document for each row of parameters from one template, as a job of kind `cohort`, each titled from a pattern ([the R7 plan](../plans/2026-10-16-r7-bulk-generation.md), R7-A, R7-C)
The rows are given inline, at most 1,000, or taken from a query result's version the caller may read, a parameter for each column (R7-B); a file is read into rows by the page

Each row is made in a savepoint of its own transaction: a refusal leaves nothing of it and is kept as the row's failure with its code and words, and the run goes on; the job's JSON Lines report has a line for every row (R7-E)

A cohort declares `onFailure` (0116): `continue`, the default, goes on past a failed row as REU-033 says; `stop` makes no more, the rows after it waiting, and Rerun runs them under the cohort's own choice; the job's outcome and the cohort's view say which it was and the row it stopped at (the R20 plan, R20-D)

Bulk generation's budget is four hundred documents from one template within an hour, measured on CI's reference runner and recorded beside it on every run, held to a tenth of it for production's margin; production's own measurement arrives with ADM-016 (T7)
As REU-033: every row reported made or failed, and a failed row leaves no document (R7-E)
A cohort is recorded with its template version, its title and its source, and `GET /v1/cohorts/{id}` names every row's document or failure to anybody who may read its space (R7-G)
`POST /v1/cohorts/{id}/rerun` sets the failed rows pending, with any corrected parameters, and runs them by a new job from the same resolution; a made row is never touched (R7-F)

The template and every definition it names are resolved once, when the cohort is asked for, and kept on it; every row, rerun or not, is made from that resolution (R7-D). Templates place no components, so no reference is movable yet

A definition's `components` names each component every document from it includes, by key, with its reference mode and its place; making a document places each as a reference carrying its key as `origin` ([Required components](#required-components))

The outline's `remove` of a reference from a required component needs a `reason`, kept as a `section_waiver` row as a section's is; a publication request with one missing and not waived is refused, `component_required`, naming its key
A required component's `place` is the start or end of a starting section, or of the top level's front matter, body or appendices by its `matter`; creation and a move place it alike

A template's query set is the definitions its required components' bindings name at the versions resolution chooses, computed, never declared (ADR-0062); making a document refuses `template_unresolved` where a component or one of those definitions is not there for the creator to read

Making a document from a template whose required components hold bindings resolves each, as the creator, before the document is made, and records each result as that binding's resolution in the transaction that makes it ([Required components](#required-components))

Each such binding's query runs when the document is made and its result is stored as a dataset version, as a resolve stores one; the binding's mode is the binding's, and the template has no setting for it

Making a document writes everything in one transaction; one whose required components run queries makes nothing until they have run, and nothing where one fails, `creation_failed`; a cohort's row is made in a savepoint of its own (R7-E)
A template parameter's `feeds.variables` names the variables it gives its value, by key: each a declared variable of its type, fed by no other parameter, else `parameter_variable` at save (R10-A)
A variable a document's template feeds takes that parameter's value when it is printed, in front of any parameter the variable names itself

Making a document from a template answers `unresolvedVariables`: each variable its required components hold that does not resolve against its parameters, values and the results it holds, by node and key, and refuses nothing

A definition's `profile` declares default values for axes and the axes a document must set; a parameter's `feeds.axis` gives its value to an axis. Making a document writes the profile, never none; a publish with a required axis unset is `profile_incomplete` ([Profile](#profile))

A cohort is found again as a set: `GET /v1/cohorts` lists every cohort in a space the caller may read, each with its template, space and rows counted made, failed and waiting, and Templates' **Cohorts** opens each one's page (the R14 plan, R14-A)

The cohort listing sorts by when asked, newest first, or by title, and filters by template and by state: complete, a row failed, or a row waiting and none failed; paged by the listing cursor (API-007)
A term holds a preferred label, alternative labels, an abbreviation, a definition and its standing
Each label and abbreviation per language
First use resolved at publish in reading order: the expansion once, the abbreviation after
Expansion is the theme's: first use, always or never
A deprecated term is flagged where it is used, its replacement named
Typing an abbreviation or a label offers the term
Broader, narrower and related terms, stated
Search reaches content through a term's labels and narrower terms
Terms exported as SKOS JSON-LD in a documented form; imported from it and from Turtle
An import reports what it could not represent
Standing is a declared workflow: draft, approved, deprecated
A language with no label falls back to the term's base language, and the fallback is reported at publish
A deprecated term is flagged as it is chosen, as well as where used (LIB-018)
A Term action on the toolbar and a shortcut apply and remove it
A glossary and a list of abbreviations generated from the terms used
As LIB-059
Terms are searchable
As LIB-060
A style is a record in a catalogue: an identifier, a name, what it applies to, and values from the property set
A catalogue is an artifact (`artifact_kind = catalogue`), versioned by the storage design, referenced by themes rather than owned by one
Catalogue kinds are fixed: paragraph, character, table, image, admonition, citation
Content carries a style identifier and nothing else about appearance; the schema has no field that could hold a property
Identifiers are allocated by the catalogue, never reused, and are what every projection keys on - the CSS class, the Typst lookup, the Word style id
Every style declares the node types it applies to; the resolver refuses a style applied outside them, naming both
`basedOn` inheritance, resolved by the resolver alone; the chain is walked with a visited set and a cycle is a named error
The paragraph property set below
A character catalogue maps each mark in CNT-031 to a rendering
That map belongs to the theme, so `strong` resolves to bold in one theme and small capitals in another
Alignment exists only as a paragraph style property; there is no field for it on a block
The table property set below, but for alignment by column type
Alignment by column type, a table style's `align`, which a bound table's column overrides (TAB-046); optional at `catalogue/3`, set by default theme 0.7 (TB1)

Default field formats by column type are a table style's `fields`, merged member by member under a bound table's column format (TAB-012, TAB-037): a number, a currency or a percentage by `style`, and a unit's brackets by `unitBrackets`; a date or a time takes the value catalogue's formats for the document's language (STY-082); optional at `catalogue/3`, set by default theme 0.7 (TB1)
An image style fixes one dimension, as points or as a fraction of the measure
The other dimension is derived from the asset's intrinsic proportions at resolution, never declared
An image style declares a maximum for the free dimension; exceeding it re-derives from that dimension instead
Placement - inline, block, floated - and alignment are image style properties

A table style and an image style placing a figure each declare `caption: 'above' \| 'below'`, required at `catalogue/3`, and the editor, the PDF and Word each set the caption on that side ([Where a caption sits](#where-a-caption-sits))

Where a caption sits is the table or image style's `caption`, and a table or a figure holds only the identifier of its style: the content model has no member for a side ([Where a caption sits](#where-a-caption-sits))

An asset version cannot be stored without its intrinsic width and height - AST records them on ingest, and the stored shape refuses a version without them - so resolution always has them. STY-019, which it supersedes, asked for a named failure that could not arise
A theme binds one catalogue of each kind, a set of typefaces, and a paper colour, and is itself an artifact
The theme a document uses is the one its template binds; the resolver is given it, never chooses
Changing a document's theme is a template-level act, audited through the lifecycle log
A style identifier the theme does not contain is a resolution error, and resolution errors fail the publish
A baseline pins the theme version; the storage design makes the pin a foreign key
Adding a style is a catalogue edit - data, validated against the schema - and involves no code
A new style is honoured everywhere because projections are generic over the property set, not written per style
A style is referenced by identifier, so its uses are a query, and deletion is refused while any exist
Catalogue edits are versions, so what changed is a comparison between two versions
A theme may carry an allowed list of style identifiers per kind; the editor offers only those, and the resolver refuses the rest
The impact of a style change is the set of documents whose pinned or floating theme version would resolve differently, listed before the change is saved
One resolver, in `packages/domain`, used by the editor and the publisher alike; the projections never resolve anything

The CSS projection is generic over the property set (STY-030), so it renders every declared paragraph and character property at the theme's values rather than a chosen few; the pagination-bound properties are the only omission, marked as such in the set and shown by preview instead of approximated (STY-037)
Properties that depend on pagination are marked as such in the property set; the CSS projection omits them and preview shows them
The resolver is a pure function of theme version, catalogue versions and asset dimensions

The pinned files are one package, `packages/fonts`, which the worker hands Typst as its only font directory and the renderer bundles for a browser and the desktop shell alike ([The theme in the editor](#the-theme-in-the-editor), ET-C)
A typeface that cannot be loaded fails resolution; Typst's missing-face warning is also treated as a failure (ADR-0013)
The typeface artifact records the licence and whether it permits embedding, separately for PDF and for Word

A catalogue serialises as its schema's JSON, which is the export format
Import validates against the schema and reports every rejected property by name
The product's own typefaces are shipped as typeface artifacts carrying their open licence
A tenant's uploaded face is a typeface artifact in that tenant's schema, so it cannot be served to anyone else
A typeface artifact is the font files themselves, versioned; the baseline pins the files
The default theme's faces are checked against Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and Hebrew and the mathematics, from their character maps, by the coverage check below

The default theme's 0.11 gives the serif Noto Naskh Arabic as its fallback (migration 0167): each text style's chain is checked against Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew and Arabic at every weight and posture, and a paragraph mixing Arabic, Hebrew and Latin is published to the PDF and Word

The domain's theme reader refuses a text colour below 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text, against any background it can stand on, and the store refuses what the reader refuses, so a theme is checked when it is saved ([Themes in the PDF](#themes-in-the-pdf), TH-G)
Vertical space between two blocks is the first block's space after plus the second block's space before, in every output
Line spacing is a minimum baseline-to-baseline distance in points, and means that distance in every output
A typeface whose licence forbids embedding in Word declares a permitted face for Word output, and the publish report names the substitution
A typeface artifact carries its ascent and descent; the CSS projection and the Typst template both use them to put a line's extra space above it
`wordRun` computes Word's reading of each run and pins the canonical value directly wherever the two differ
The CSS projection renders block spacing by the same rule as the output (STY-050)

The editor loads the theme's typefaces and sets text at the theme's sizes
The editor sets text at the layout's measure, scaled, with zoom

A style missing or out of place, a face the renderer does not hold and a character its family cannot set are each marked on the text, never set in a silent default ([The theme in the editor](#the-theme-in-the-editor), ET-I)

The browser suite measures the editor against the PDF of the same document under the default theme, a contrary one and three generated from seeds: every length within half a point, and every face, weight, posture, colour, underline and fill exactly, with STY-060's list of approved deviations between the two empty ([The theme in the editor, measured](#the-theme-in-the-editor-measured))
Embedding in PDF and in Word is decided per face from its licence (STY-041, STY-042, STY-052)
The Word projection emits every style as a real Word style, named and identified from the catalogue
A table breaks across pages as its table style says - header repeated, rows kept whole, a continuation label - which the template sets from the style ([Themes in the PDF](#themes-in-the-pdf), TH-I)
